<h1 id="paddle-api">Paddle API v1.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

The Paddle API lets you create, read, and update information in your Paddle Billing system.

Paddle Billing is a complete subscription and recurring revenue management platform, designed for modern SaaS businesses. It helps you increase your revenue, retain customers, and scale your operations.

The Paddle API lets you create, read, and update information in your Paddle Billing system. You can use it to integrate Paddle with your app or third-party solutions.

See https://developer.paddle.com/ to learn more.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://sandbox-api.paddle.com">https://sandbox-api.paddle.com</a> - Sandbox

* <a href="https://api.paddle.com">https://api.paddle.com</a> - Live

# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer Requests are authenticated with API keys. Provide your API key as a Bearer token in the Authorization header.

API keys are assigned permissions, granting them access to entities and operations.
Each endpoint may require one or more permissions, defined with the `x-permissions` extension.
Values for include parameters may require specific permissions as defined in the `x-enum-permissions` extension.
See all available permissions in the apikey-permission schema or [documentation](https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/about/permissions).

Get an API key and select the permissions you need from the Paddle dashboard under [Paddle > My account > Settings > Authentication](https://vendors.paddle.com/settings/authentication).

<h1 id="paddle-api-verifications">Verifications</h1>

Verification entities show whether an account is ready for live payments, and which steps are still outstanding. They're read-only.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/verifications">Verifications overview</a>

## List verifications

<a id="opIdlist-verifications"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/verifications \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /verifications`

Returns a paginated list of verifications. Use the query parameters to page through results.

Filter by `verification_type=onboarding` and use the returned verification's `status` to check whether your account is ready for live payments or needs action.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/verifications/list-verifications">List verifications</a>

<h3 id="list-verifications-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|query|[string]|false|Return only the IDs specified. Use a comma-separated list to get multiple entities.|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `50`; Maximum: `200`.|
|verification_type|query|[VerificationType](#schemaverificationtype)|false|Filter verifications by type. If omitted, verifications of all types are returned.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Order returned entities by the specified field and direction (`[ASC]` or `[DESC]`). For example, `?order_by=id[ASC]`.<br><br>Valid fields for ordering: `id`.|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|verification_type|onboarding|
|verification_type|domain|

## Get a verification

<a id="opIdget-verification"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/verifications/slrvrf_01gjn16x6xxb6vkznqwfphthxb \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /verifications/{verification_id}`

Returns a verification using its ID.

The response includes the verification steps.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/verifications/get-verification">Get a verification</a>

<h3 id="get-a-verification-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|verification_id|path|[VerificationId](#schemaverificationid)|true|none|

<h1 id="paddle-api-transactions">Transactions</h1>

Transaction entities calculate and capture revenue. They hold information about an amount that you're billing for.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/transactions">Transaction entity overview</a>

## List transactions

<a id="opIdlist-transactions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/transactions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /transactions`

Returns a paginated list of transactions. Use the query parameters to page through results.

Use the `include` parameter to include related entities in the response.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/transactions/list-transactions">List transactions</a>

<h3 id="list-transactions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include|query|[[TransactionIncludeQuery](#schematransactionincludequery)]|false|Include related entities in the response. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple entities.|
|id|query|[string]|false|Return only the IDs specified. Use a comma-separated list to get multiple entities.|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|billed_at|query|string|false|Return entities billed at a specific time. Pass an RFC 3339 datetime string, or use `[LT]` (less than), `[LTE]` (less than or equal to), `[GT]` (greater than), or `[GTE]` (greater than or equal to) operators. For example, `billed_at=2023-04-18T17:03:26` or `billed_at[LT]=2023-04-18T17:03:26`.|
|collection_mode|query|[CollectionMode](#schemacollectionmode)|false|Return entities that match the specified collection mode.|
|created_at|query|string|false|Return entities created at a specific time. Pass an RFC 3339 datetime string, or use `[LT]` (less than), `[LTE]` (less than or equal to), `[GT]` (greater than), or `[GTE]` (greater than or equal to) operators. For example, `created_at=2023-04-18T17:03:26` or `created_at[LT]=2023-04-18T17:03:26`.|
|customer_id|query|[string]|false|Return entities related to the specified customer. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple customer IDs.|
|invoice_number|query|[string]|false|Return entities that match the invoice number. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple invoice numbers.|
|origin|query|[[TransactionOriginQuery](#schematransactionoriginquery)]|false|Return entities related to the specified origin. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple origins.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Order returned entities by the specified field and direction (`[ASC]` or `[DESC]`). For example, `?order_by=id[ASC]`.<br><br>Valid fields for ordering: `billed_at`, `created_at`, `id`, and `updated_at`.|
|status|query|[[TransactionStatusQuery](#schematransactionstatusquery)]|false|Return entities that match the specified status. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple status values.|
|subscription_id|query|[string] \| null|false|Return entities related to the specified subscription. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple subscription IDs. Pass `null` to return entities that aren't related to any subscription.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `30`; Maximum: `30`.|
|updated_at|query|string|false|Return entities updated at a specific time. Pass an RFC 3339 datetime string, or use `[LT]` (less than), `[LTE]` (less than or equal to), `[GT]` (greater than), or `[GTE]` (greater than or equal to) operators. For example, `updated_at=2023-04-18T17:03:26` or `updated_at[LT]=2023-04-18T17:03:26`.|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|include|address|
|include|adjustments|
|include|adjustments_totals|
|include|available_payment_methods|

|origin|web|

|status|billed|
|status|paid|
|status|completed|
|status|canceled|
|status|past_due|

## Create a transaction

<a id="opIdcreate-transaction"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/transactions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "items": [
      {
        "quantity": 20,
        "price_id": "pri_01gsz91wy9k1yn7kx82aafwvea"
      },
      {
        "quantity": 1,
        "price_id": "pri_01gsz96z29d88jrmsf2ztbfgjg"
      },
      {
        "quantity": 1,
        "price_id": "pri_01gsz98e27ak2tyhexptwc58yk"
      }
    ],
    "customer_id": "ctm_01hv6y1jedq4p1n0yqn5ba3ky4",
    "address_id": "add_01hv8gq3318ktkfengj2r75gfx",
    "currency_code": "USD",
    "collection_mode": "manual",
    "billing_details": {
      "enable_checkout": false,
      "purchase_order_number": "PO-123",
      "payment_terms": {
        "interval": "day",
        "frequency": 14
      }
    },
    "billing_period": {
      "starts_at": "2024-04-12T00:00:00Z",
      "ends_at": "2025-04-11T23:59:00Z"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /transactions`

Creates a new transaction.

Transactions are typically created with the status of `draft` or `ready` initially:

* Draft transactions have `items` against them, but don't have all of the required fields for billing. Paddle creates draft transactions automatically when a checkout is opened.
* Paddle automatically marks transactions as `ready` when all of the required fields are present for billing. This includes `customer_id` and `address_id` for automatically-collected transactions, and `billing_details` for manually-collected transactions.

The `collection_mode` against a transaction determines how Paddle tries to collect for payment:

* Manually-collected transactions are for sales-assisted billing. Paddle sends an invoice to your customer when a transaction is `billed`. Payment is often by wire transfer.
* Automatically-collected transactions are for self-serve checkouts. You may pass the transaction to a checkout or use the returned `checkout.url` to collect for payment.

When a manually-collected transaction is marked as `billed` or an automatically-collected transaction is `completed`, Paddle automatically creates a related subscription for the items on the transaction.

If successful, your response includes a copy of the new transaction entity.

Use the `include` parameter to include related entities in the response.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/transactions/create-transaction">Create a transaction</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "quantity": 20,
      "price_id": "pri_01gsz91wy9k1yn7kx82aafwvea"
    },
    {
      "quantity": 1,
      "price_id": "pri_01gsz96z29d88jrmsf2ztbfgjg"
    },
    {
      "quantity": 1,
      "price_id": "pri_01gsz98e27ak2tyhexptwc58yk"
    }
  ],
  "customer_id": "ctm_01hv6y1jedq4p1n0yqn5ba3ky4",
  "address_id": "add_01hv8gq3318ktkfengj2r75gfx",
  "currency_code": "USD",
  "collection_mode": "manual",
  "billing_details": {
    "enable_checkout": false,
    "purchase_order_number": "PO-123",
    "payment_terms": {
      "interval": "day",
      "frequency": 14
    }
  },
  "billing_period": {
    "starts_at": "2024-04-12T00:00:00Z",
    "ends_at": "2025-04-11T23:59:00Z"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-transaction-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include|query|[[TransactionIncludeQuery](#schematransactionincludequery)]|false|Include related entities in the response. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple entities.|
|body|body|[TransactionCreate](#schematransactioncreate)|true|none|
|» status|body|object|false|Status of this transaction. You may set a transaction to `billed` when creating,<br>or omit to let Paddle set the status. Transactions are created as `ready` if they have<br>an `address_id`, `customer_id`, and `items`, otherwise they are created as `draft`.<br><br>Marking as `billed` when creating is typically used when working with manually-collected<br>transactions as part of an invoicing workflow. Billed transactions cannot be updated, only canceled.|
|» customer_id|body|[CustomerId](#schemacustomerid) \| null|false|Paddle ID of the customer that this transaction is for, prefixed with `ctm_`. If omitted, transaction status is `draft`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[CustomerId](#schemacustomerid)|false|Unique Paddle ID for this customer entity, prefixed with `ctm_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» address_id|body|[AddressId](#schemaaddressid) \| null|false|Paddle ID of the address that this transaction is for, prefixed with `add_`. Requires `customer_id`. If omitted, transaction status is `draft`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[AddressId](#schemaaddressid)|false|Unique Paddle ID for this address entity, prefixed with `add_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» business_id|body|[BusinessId](#schemabusinessid) \| null|false|Paddle ID of the business that this transaction is for, prefixed with `biz_`. Requires `customer_id`. |
|» » *anyOf*|body|[BusinessId](#schemabusinessid)|false|Unique Paddle ID for this business entity, prefixed with `biz_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» custom_data|body|[CustomData](#schemacustomdata) \| null|false|Your own structured key-value data.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[CustomData](#schemacustomdata)|false|Your own structured key-value data.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» currency_code|body|[CurrencyCode](#schemacurrencycode) \| null|false|Supported three-letter ISO 4217 currency code. Must be `USD`, `EUR`, or `GBP` if `collection_mode` is `manual`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[CurrencyCode](#schemacurrencycode)|false|Supported three-letter ISO 4217 currency code.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» origin|body|object|false|none|
|» subscription_id|body|[SubscriptionId](#schemasubscriptionid) \| null|false|Paddle ID of the subscription that this transaction is for, prefixed with `sub_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[SubscriptionId](#schemasubscriptionid)|false|Unique Paddle ID for this subscription entity, prefixed with `sub_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» collection_mode|body|object|false|How payment is collected for this transaction. `automatic` for checkout, `manual` for invoices. If omitted, defaults to `automatic`.|
|» discount_id|body|[DiscountId](#schemadiscountid) \| null|false|Paddle ID of the discount to apply to this transaction, prefixed with `dsc_`. Send one of `discount_id` or `discount`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[DiscountId](#schemadiscountid)|false|Unique Paddle ID for this discount, prefixed with `dsc_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» discount|body|[DiscountCustom](#schemadiscountcustom) \| null|false|Apply a non-catalog discount to a transaction. Send one of `discount_id` or `discount`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[DiscountCustom](#schemadiscountcustom)|false|Represents a discount entity for a custom, non-catalog discount.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» billing_details|body|[BillingDetailsCreate](#schemabillingdetailscreate) \| null|false|Details for invoicing. Required if `collection_mode` is `manual`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[BillingDetailsCreate](#schemabillingdetailscreate)|false|Details for invoicing. Required if `collection_mode` is `manual`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» billing_period|body|[TimePeriod](#schematimeperiod) \| null|false|Time period that this transaction is for. Set automatically by Paddle for subscription renewals to describe the period that charges are for.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[TimePeriod](#schematimeperiod)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» items|body|[[TransactionItemCreate](#schematransactionitemcreate)]|true|List of items to charge for. You can charge for items that you've added to your catalog by passing the Paddle ID of an existing price entity, or you can charge for non-catalog items by passing a price object.<br><br>Non-catalog items can be for existing products, or you can pass a product object as part of your price to charge for a non-catalog product.|
|» checkout|body|[TransactionCheckoutCreate](#schematransactioncheckoutcreate) \| null|false|Paddle Checkout details for this transaction. You may pass a URL when creating or updating an automatically-collected transaction, or when creating or updating a manually-collected transaction where `billing_details.enable_checkout` is `true`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[TransactionCheckoutCreate](#schematransactioncheckoutcreate)|false|Paddle Checkout details for this transaction. You may pass a URL when creating or updating an automatically-collected transaction, or when creating or updating a manually-collected transaction where `billing_details.enable_checkout` is `true`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

Use the `include` parameter to include related entities in the response.

## Update a transaction

<a id="opIdupdate-transaction"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/transactions/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "discount_id": "dsc_01gtgztp8fpchantd5g1wrksa3",
    "items": [
      {
        "quantity": 50,
        "price_id": "pri_01gsz91wy9k1yn7kx82aafwvea"
      },
      {
        "quantity": 1,
        "price_id": "pri_01gsz96z29d88jrmsf2ztbfgjg"
      },
      {
        "quantity": 1,
        "price_id": "pri_01gsz98e27ak2tyhexptwc58yk"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /transactions/{transaction_id}`

Updates a transaction using its ID.

You can update transactions that are `draft` or `ready`. `billed` and `completed` transactions are considered records for tax and legal purposes, so they can't be changed. You can either:

* Create [an adjustment](https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/adjustments/overview) to record a refund or credit for a transaction.
* Cancel a `billed` transaction by sending a PATCH request to set `status` to `canceled`.

You can cancel transactions that are `draft`, `ready`, `billed`, or `past_due`. When canceling, only include `status` in your request. You can't use the API to cancel transactions that Paddle created for a subscription, where `origin` starts with `subscription_`, or automatically-collected transactions that are `past_due`. Cancel transactions created for a subscription using the Paddle dashboard.

The transaction `status` may only be set to `billed` or `canceled`. Other statuses are set automatically by Paddle. Set a manually-collected transaction to `billed` to mark it as finalized. This is essentially issuing an invoice. At this point, it becomes a legal record so you can't make changes to it, only cancel it. Paddle automatically assigns an invoice number, creates [a related subscription](https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/subscriptions/overview), and sends it to your customer.

When making changes to items on a transaction, send the complete list of items that you'd like to be on a transaction — including existing items. For each item, send an object containing `price_id` and `quantity`. Paddle responds with the full `price` object for each item. See: [Work with lists](https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/about/lists)

If successful, your response includes a copy of the updated transaction entity.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/transactions/update-transaction">Update a transaction</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "discount_id": "dsc_01gtgztp8fpchantd5g1wrksa3",
  "items": [
    {
      "quantity": 50,
      "price_id": "pri_01gsz91wy9k1yn7kx82aafwvea"
    },
    {
      "quantity": 1,
      "price_id": "pri_01gsz96z29d88jrmsf2ztbfgjg"
    },
    {
      "quantity": 1,
      "price_id": "pri_01gsz98e27ak2tyhexptwc58yk"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-transaction-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include|query|[[TransactionIncludeQuery](#schematransactionincludequery)]|false|Include related entities in the response. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple entities.|
|transaction_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the transaction entity to work with.|
|body|body|[UpdateTransaction](#schemaupdatetransaction)|true|none|
|» status|body|object|false|Status of this transaction. You may set a transaction to `billed` or `canceled`. Billed transactions cannot be updated, only canceled.<br><br>For manually-collected transactions, marking as `billed` is essentially issuing an invoice.<br><br>You can cancel transactions that are `draft`, `ready`, `billed`, or `past_due`, except transactions that Paddle created for a subscription and automatically-collected transactions that are `past_due`.|
|» customer_id|body|[CustomerId](#schemacustomerid) \| null|false|Paddle ID of the customer that this transaction is for, prefixed with `ctm_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[CustomerId](#schemacustomerid)|false|Unique Paddle ID for this customer entity, prefixed with `ctm_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» address_id|body|[AddressId](#schemaaddressid) \| null|false|Paddle ID of the address that this transaction is for, prefixed with `add_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[AddressId](#schemaaddressid)|false|Unique Paddle ID for this address entity, prefixed with `add_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» business_id|body|[BusinessId](#schemabusinessid) \| null|false|Paddle ID of the business that this transaction is for, prefixed with `biz_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[BusinessId](#schemabusinessid)|false|Unique Paddle ID for this business entity, prefixed with `biz_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» custom_data|body|[CustomData](#schemacustomdata) \| null|false|Your own structured key-value data.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[CustomData](#schemacustomdata)|false|Your own structured key-value data.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» currency_code|body|[CurrencyCode](#schemacurrencycode) \| null|false|Supported three-letter ISO 4217 currency code. Must be `USD`, `EUR`, or `GBP` if `collection_mode` is `manual`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[CurrencyCode](#schemacurrencycode)|false|Supported three-letter ISO 4217 currency code.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» origin|body|[PublicTransactionOrigin](#schemapublictransactionorigin)|false|none|
|» subscription_id|body|[SubscriptionId](#schemasubscriptionid) \| null|false|Paddle ID of the subscription that this transaction is for, prefixed with `sub_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[SubscriptionId](#schemasubscriptionid)|false|Unique Paddle ID for this subscription entity, prefixed with `sub_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» collection_mode|body|object|false|How payment is collected for this transaction. `automatic` for checkout, `manual` for invoices.|
|» discount_id|body|[DiscountId](#schemadiscountid) \| null|false|Paddle ID of the discount to apply to this transaction, prefixed with `dsc_`. Send one of `discount_id` or `discount`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[DiscountId](#schemadiscountid)|false|Unique Paddle ID for this discount, prefixed with `dsc_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» discount|body|[DiscountCustom](#schemadiscountcustom) \| null|false|Apply a non-catalog discount to a transaction. Send one of `discount_id` or `discount`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[DiscountCustom](#schemadiscountcustom)|false|Represents a discount entity for a custom, non-catalog discount.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» billing_details|body|[BillingDetailsUpdate](#schemabillingdetailsupdate) \| null|false|Details for invoicing. Required if `collection_mode` is `manual`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[BillingDetailsUpdate](#schemabillingdetailsupdate)|false|Details for invoicing. Required if `collection_mode` is `manual`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» billing_period|body|[TimePeriod](#schematimeperiod) \| null|false|Time period that this transaction is for. Set automatically by Paddle for subscription renewals to describe the period that charges are for.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[TimePeriod](#schematimeperiod)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» items|body|[[TransactionItemUpdate](#schematransactionitemupdate)]|false|List of items on this transaction.<br><br>When making a request, each object must contain either a `price_id` or a `price` object, and a `quantity`.<br><br>Include a `price_id` to charge for an existing catalog item, or a `price` object to charge for a non-catalog item.|

You may pass a URL when creating or updating an automatically-collected transaction, or when creating or updating a manually-collected transaction where `billing_details.enable_checkout` is `true`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[TransactionCheckoutCreate](#schematransactioncheckoutcreate)|false|Paddle Checkout details for this transaction. You may pass a URL when creating or updating an automatically-collected transaction, or when creating or updating a manually-collected transaction where `billing_details.enable_checkout` is `true`.|

## Preview a transaction

<a id="opIdpreview-transaction-create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/transactions/preview \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "items": [
      {
        "quantity": 20,
        "price_id": "pri_01gsz8x8sawmvhz1pv30nge1ke"
      },
      {
        "quantity": 1,
        "price_id": "pri_01h1vjfevh5etwq3rb416a23h2"
      },
      {
        "quantity": 1,
        "price_id": "pri_01gsz98e27ak2tyhexptwc58yk",
        "include_in_totals": false
      }
    ],
    "discount_id": "dsc_01gtgztp8fpchantd5g1wrksa3",
    "address": {
      "country_code": "US"
    },
    "currency_code": "USD"
  }'
```

`POST /transactions/preview`

Previews a transaction without creating a transaction entity. Typically used for creating more advanced, dynamic pricing pages where users can build their own plans.

Consider using [the preview prices operation](https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/pricing-preview/preview-prices) for simpler pricing pages.

You can provide location information when previewing a transaction. You must provide this if you want Paddle to calculate tax or [automatically localize prices](https://developer.paddle.com/build/products/offer-localized-pricing). You can provide one of:

* `customer_ip_address`: Paddle fetches location using the IP address to calculate totals.
* `address`: Paddle uses the country and ZIP code (where supplied) to calculate totals.
* `customer_id`, `address_id`, `business_id`: Paddle uses existing customer data to calculate totals. Typically used for logged-in customers.

When supplying items, you can exclude items from the total calculation using the `include_in_totals` boolean.

By default, recurring items with trials are considered to have a zero charge when previewing. Set `ignore_trials` to `true` to ignore trial periods against prices for transaction preview calculations.

If successful, your response includes the data you sent with a `details` object that includes totals for the supplied prices.

Transaction previews don't create transactions, so no `id` is returned.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/transactions/preview-transaction-create">Preview a transaction</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "quantity": 20,
      "price_id": "pri_01gsz8x8sawmvhz1pv30nge1ke"
    },
    {
      "quantity": 1,
      "price_id": "pri_01h1vjfevh5etwq3rb416a23h2"
    },
    {
      "quantity": 1,
      "price_id": "pri_01gsz98e27ak2tyhexptwc58yk",
      "include_in_totals": false
    }
  ],
  "discount_id": "dsc_01gtgztp8fpchantd5g1wrksa3",
  "address": {
    "country_code": "US"
  },
  "currency_code": "USD"
}
```

<h3 id="preview-a-transaction-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransactionPreviewCreate](#schematransactionpreviewcreate)|true|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[TransactionPreviewCreateWithoutAddress](#schematransactionpreviewcreatewithoutaddress)|false|Preview a transaction without using any address information.|
|» *anyOf*|body|[TransactionPreviewCreateAddress](#schematransactionpreviewcreateaddress)|false|Paddle uses the country and ZIP code (where supplied) to calculate totals.|
|» *anyOf*|body|[TransactionPreviewCreateIpAddress](#schematransactionpreviewcreateipaddress)|false|Paddle fetches location using the IP address to calculate totals.|
|» *anyOf*|body|[TransactionPreviewCreatePaddleIds](#schematransactionpreviewcreatepaddleids)|false|Paddle uses existing customer data to calculate totals. Typically used for logged-in customers.|

## Revise customer information on a billed or completed transaction

<a id="opIdrevise-transaction"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/transactions/string/revise \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "customer": {
      "name": "Sam Miller"
    },
    "business": {
      "tax_identifier": "AB0123456789"
    },
    "address": {
      "first_line": "3811 Ditmars Blvd"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /transactions/{transaction_id}/revise`

Revises customer information for a billed or completed transaction.

Revise a transaction to rectify incorrect customer, address, or business information on invoice documents generated by Paddle.

You can revise transaction details that don't impact the tax rates on a transaction. This includes:

* Customer name
* Business name and tax or VAT number (`tax_identifier`)
* Address details, apart from the country

You can't remove a valid tax or VAT number, only replace it with another valid one. If a valid tax or VAT number is added, Paddle automatically creates an adjustment to refund any tax where applicable.

Transactions can only be revised once.

If successful, your response includes a copy of the transaction entity. [Get a transaction](https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/transactions/get-transaction) using the `include` parameter with the `customer`, `address`, and `business` values to see the revised customer information.

Only the customer information for this transaction is updated. The related customer, address, and business entities aren't updated.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/transactions/revise-transaction">Revise a transaction</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "customer": {
    "name": "Sam Miller"
  },
  "business": {
    "tax_identifier": "AB0123456789"
  },
  "address": {
    "first_line": "3811 Ditmars Blvd"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="revise-customer-information-on-a-billed-or-completed-transaction-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transaction_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the transaction entity to work with.|
|body|body|[TransactionRevise](#schematransactionrevise)|true|none|
|» customer|body|object|false|Revised customer information for this transaction.|
|» » name|body|object|false|Revised name of the customer for this transaction.|
|» business|body|object|false|Revised business information for this transaction.|
|» » name|body|object|false|Revised name of the business for this transaction.|
|» » tax_identifier|body|string|false|Revised tax or VAT number for this transaction. You can't remove a valid tax or VAT number, only replace it with another valid one. Paddle automatically creates an adjustment to refund any tax where applicable.|
|» address|body|object|false|Revised address information for this transaction.|
|» » first_line|body|string|false|Revised first line of the address for this transaction.|
|» » second_line|body|string \| null|false|Revised second line of the address for this transaction.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» » city|body|string|false|Revised city of the address for this transaction.|
|» » region|body|string|false|Revised state, county, or region of the address for this transaction.|

## Get a PDF invoice for a transaction

<a id="opIdget-transaction-invoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/transactions/string/invoice \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /transactions/{transaction_id}/invoice`

Returns a link to an invoice PDF for a transaction.

Invoice PDFs are available for both automatically and manually-collected transactions:

* The PDF for manually-collected transactions includes payment terms, purchase order number, and notes for your customer. It's a demand for payment from your customer. It's available for transactions that are `billed` or `completed`.
* The PDF for automatically-collected transactions lets your customer know that payment was taken successfully. Customers may require this for for tax-reporting purposes. It's available for transactions that are `completed`.

Invoice PDFs aren't available for zero-value transactions.

The link returned is not a permanent link. It expires after an hour.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/transactions/get-invoice-pdf">Get a PDF invoice for a transaction</a>

<h3 id="get-a-pdf-invoice-for-a-transaction-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transaction_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the transaction entity to work with.|
|disposition|query|[Disposition](#schemadisposition)|false|Determine whether the generated URL should download the PDF as an attachment saved locally, or open it inline in the browser.<br><br>Default: `attachment`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|disposition|attachment|
|disposition|inline|

  "data": {
    "url": "https://paddle-production-invoice-service-pdfs.s3.amazonaws.com/invoices/10889/e01ae945-9e6d-4208-a0ba-83b107e06657/invoice_325-10650_DX-ChatApp.pdf"
  },
  "meta": {
    "request_id": "126c131a-258a-482b-b4a9-9ffca5126539"
  }
}

<h1 id="paddle-api-subscriptions">Subscriptions</h1>

Subscription entities describe a recurring billing relationship with a customer. They're closely related to transactions.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/subscriptions">Subscription entity overview</a>

## List subscriptions

<a id="opIdlist-subscriptions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/subscriptions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /subscriptions`

Returns a paginated list of subscriptions. Use the query parameters to page through results.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/subscriptions/list-subscriptions">List subscriptions</a>

<h3 id="list-subscriptions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|query|[string]|false|Return only the IDs specified. Use a comma-separated list to get multiple entities.|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `50`; Maximum: `200`.|
|address_id|query|[string]|false|Return entities related to the specified address. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple address IDs.|
|collection_mode|query|[CollectionModeQuery](#schemacollectionmodequery)|false|Return entities that match the specified collection mode.|
|customer_id|query|[string]|false|Return entities related to the specified customer. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple customer IDs.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Order returned entities by the specified field and direction (`[ASC]` or `[DESC]`). For example, `?order_by=id[ASC]`.<br><br>Valid fields for ordering: `id`.|
|price_id|query|[string]|false|Return entities related to the specified price. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple price IDs.|
|scheduled_change_action|query|[[ScheduledChangeActionQuery](#schemascheduledchangeactionquery)]|false|Return subscriptions that have a scheduled change. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple scheduled change actions.|
|next_billed_at|query|[string] \| null|false|Return entities next billed at a specific time. Pass `null` to return entities with no next billing date.<br>|
|status|query|[[SubscriptionStatusQuery](#schemasubscriptionstatusquery)]|false|Return entities that match the specified status. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple status values.|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

|---|---|

|collection_mode|manual|
|scheduled_change_action|cancel|
|scheduled_change_action|pause|
|scheduled_change_action|resume|
|scheduled_change_action|none|
|status|active|
|status|canceled|
|status|past_due|
|status|paused|
|status|trialing|

## Get a subscription

<a id="opIdget-subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/subscriptions/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /subscriptions/{subscription_id}`

Returns a subscription using its ID.

Use the `include` parameter to include transaction information in the response.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/subscriptions/get-subscription">Get a subscription</a>

<h3 id="get-a-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include|query|[[SubscriptionIncludeEnum](#schemasubscriptionincludeenum)]|false|Include related entities in the response. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple entities.|
|subscription_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the subscription entity to work with.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|include|next_transaction|
|include|recurring_transaction_details|

## Update a subscription

<a id="opIdupdate-subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/subscriptions/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "items": [
      {
        "price_id": "pri_01gsz8x8sawmvhz1pv30nge1ke",
        "quantity": 20
      },
      {
        "price_id": "pri_01h1vjfevh5etwq3rb416a23h2",
        "quantity": 1
      },
      {
        "price_id": "pri_01gsz95g2zrkagg294kpstx54r",
        "quantity": 1
      }
    ],
    "proration_billing_mode": "prorated_immediately"
  }'
```

`PATCH /subscriptions/{subscription_id}`

Updates a subscription using its ID.

When making changes to items or the next billing date for a subscription, you must include the `proration_billing_mode` field to tell Paddle how to bill for those changes.

Send the complete list of items that you'd like to be on a subscription — including existing items. If you omit items, they're removed from the subscription.

For each item, send `price_id` and `quantity`. Paddle responds with the full price object for each price. If you're updating an existing item, you can omit the `quantity` if you don't want to update it.

If successful, your response includes a copy of the updated subscription entity. When an update results in an immediate charge, responses may take longer than usual while a payment attempt is processed.

You can't update a subscription that's `past_due`, except to remove a scheduled change by setting `scheduled_change` to `null`.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/subscriptions/update-subscription">Update a subscription</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "price_id": "pri_01gsz8x8sawmvhz1pv30nge1ke",
      "quantity": 20
    },
    {
      "price_id": "pri_01h1vjfevh5etwq3rb416a23h2",
      "quantity": 1
    },
    {
      "price_id": "pri_01gsz95g2zrkagg294kpstx54r",
      "quantity": 1
    }
  ],
  "proration_billing_mode": "prorated_immediately"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the subscription entity to work with.|
|body|body|[SubscriptionUpdate](#schemasubscriptionupdate)|true|none|
|» customer_id|body|object|false|Paddle ID of the customer that this subscription is for, prefixed with `ctm_`. Include to change the customer for a subscription.|
|» address_id|body|object|false|Paddle ID of the address that this subscription is for, prefixed with `add_`. Include to change the address for a subscription.|
|» business_id|body|[BusinessId](#schemabusinessid) \| null|false|Paddle ID of the business that this subscription is for, prefixed with `biz_`. Include to change the business for a subscription.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[BusinessId](#schemabusinessid)|false|Unique Paddle ID for this business entity, prefixed with `biz_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» currency_code|body|object|false|Supported three-letter ISO 4217 currency code. Include to change the currency that a subscription bills in. When changing `collection_mode` to `manual`, you may need to change currency code to `USD`, `EUR`, or `GBP`.|
|» next_billed_at|body|object|false|RFC 3339 datetime string of when this subscription is next scheduled to be billed. Include to change the next billing date.|
|» discount|body|[SubscriptionUpdateDiscount](#schemasubscriptionupdatediscount) \| null|false|Details of the discount applied to this subscription. Include to add a discount to a subscription. `null` to remove a discount.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[SubscriptionUpdateDiscount](#schemasubscriptionupdatediscount)|false|Details of the discount applied to this subscription. Include to add a discount to a subscription. `null` to remove a discount.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» collection_mode|body|object|false|How payment is collected for transactions created for this subscription. `automatic` for checkout, `manual` for invoices.|
|» billing_details|body|[BillingDetailsUpdate](#schemabillingdetailsupdate) \| null|false|Details for invoicing. Required if `collection_mode` is `manual`. `null` if changing `collection_mode` to `automatic`.|

|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

## Cancel a subscription

<a id="opIdcancel-subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/subscriptions/string/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "effective_from": "immediately"
  }'
```

`POST /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/cancel`

Cancels a subscription using its ID.

By default, active subscriptions are canceled at the end of the billing period. When you send a request to cancel, Paddle creates a `scheduled_change` against the subscription entity to say that it should cancel at the end of the current billing period. Its `status` remains `active` until after the effective date of the scheduled change, at which point it changes to `canceled`.

You can cancel a subscription right away by including `effective_from` in your request, setting the value to `immediately`. If successful, your response includes a copy of the updated subscription entity with the `status` of `canceled`. Paused subscriptions can only be canceled immediately, so you must set `effective_from` to `immediately` to cancel them.

You can cancel subscriptions that are `past_due`. If you cancel at the end of the billing period, the `status` remains `past_due` until the end of the current billing period. Cancel immediately to stop the subscription right away.

You can't reinstate a canceled subscription.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/subscriptions/cancel-subscription">Cancel a subscription</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "effective_from": "immediately"
}
```

<h3 id="cancel-a-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the subscription entity to work with.|
|body|body|[SubscriptionCancel](#schemasubscriptioncancel)|true|none|
|» effective_from|body|[EffectiveFrom](#schemaeffectivefrom) \| null|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[EffectiveFrom](#schemaeffectivefrom)|false|When this subscription change should take effect from. Defaults to `next_billing_period`, which creates a<br>`scheduled_change` to apply the subscription change at the end of the billing period.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *anyOf*|next_billing_period|
|» » *anyOf*|immediately|

## Pause a subscription

<a id="opIdpause-subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/subscriptions/string/pause \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "effective_from": "next_billing_period",
    "resume_at": "2024-09-01T16:30:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/pause`

Pauses a subscription using its ID.

By default, subscriptions are paused at the end of the billing period. When you send a request to pause, Paddle creates a `scheduled_change` against the subscription entity to say that it should pause at the end of the current billing period. Its `status` remains `active` until after the effective date of the scheduled change, at which point it changes to `paused`.

You can pause a subscription right away by including `effective_from` in your request, setting the value to `immediately`. If successful, your response includes a copy of the updated subscription entity with the `status` of `paused`.

To set a resume date, include the `resume_at` field in your request. The subscription remains paused until the resume date, or until you send a resume request. Omit to create an open-ended pause. The subscription remains paused indefinitely, until you send a resume request.

You can pause subscriptions that are `past_due`, but you can't set `on_resume` to `continue_existing_billing_period` for them.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/subscriptions/pause-subscription">Pause a subscription</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "effective_from": "next_billing_period",
  "resume_at": "2024-09-01T16:30:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="pause-a-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the subscription entity to work with.|
|body|body|[SubscriptionPause](#schemasubscriptionpause)|true|none|
|» effective_from|body|[EffectiveFrom](#schemaeffectivefrom) \| null|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[EffectiveFrom](#schemaeffectivefrom)|false|When this subscription change should take effect from. Defaults to `next_billing_period`, which creates a<br>`scheduled_change` to apply the subscription change at the end of the billing period.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» resume_at|body|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp) \| null|false|RFC 3339 datetime string of when the paused subscription should resume. Omit to pause indefinitely until resumed.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[Timestamp](#schematimestamp)|false|RFC 3339 datetime string.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» on_resume|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *anyOf*|next_billing_period|
|» » *anyOf*|immediately|

## Resume a paused subscription

<a id="opIdresume-subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/subscriptions/string/resume \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "effective_from": "immediately"
  }'
```

`POST /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/resume`

Resumes a paused subscription using its ID. Only `paused` subscriptions can be resumed. If an `active` subscription has a scheduled change to pause in the future, use this operation to set or change the resume date.

You can't resume a `canceled` subscription.

On resume, Paddle bills for a subscription immediately by default. Subscription billing dates are recalculated based on the resume date. Use the `on_resume` field to change this behavior.

If successful, Paddle returns a copy of the updated subscription entity:

* When resuming a `paused` subscription immediately, the subscription status is `active`, and billing dates are updated to reflect the resume date.
* When scheduling a `paused` subscription to resume on a date in the future, the subscription status is `paused`, and `scheduled_change.action` is `resume` with `scheduled_change.effective_at` set to the scheduled resume date.
* When changing the resume date for an `active` subscription that's scheduled to pause, the subscription status remains `active`, and `scheduled_change.resume_at` is updated on the existing `pause` scheduled change.

This operation may result in an immediate charge, so responses may take longer than usual while a payment attempt is processed.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/subscriptions/resume-subscription">Resume a paused subscription</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "effective_from": "immediately"
}
```

<h3 id="resume-a-paused-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the subscription entity to work with.|
|body|body|[SubscriptionResume](#schemasubscriptionresume)|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[SubscriptionResumeOnDate](#schemasubscriptionresumeondate)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[SubscriptionResumeImmediately](#schemasubscriptionresumeimmediately)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[EmptyObject](#schemaemptyobject)|false|none|

## Activate a trialing subscription

<a id="opIdactivate-subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/subscriptions/string/activate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/activate`

Activates a trialing subscription using its ID. Only automatically-collected subscriptions where the status is `trialing` can be activated.

On activation, Paddle bills for a subscription immediately. Subscription billing dates are recalculated based on the activation date (the time the activation request is made).

If successful, Paddle returns a copy of the updated subscription entity. The subscription status is `active`, and billing dates are updated to reflect the activation date.

This operation results in an immediate charge, so responses may take longer than usual while a payment attempt is processed.

## Get a transaction to update payment method

<a id="opIdget-subscription-update-payment-method-transaction"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/subscriptions/string/update-payment-method-transaction \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/update-payment-method-transaction`

Returns a transaction that you can pass to a checkout to let customers update their payment details. Only for subscriptions where `collection_mode` is `automatic`.

The transaction returned depends on the status of the related subscription:

* Where a subscription is `past_due`, it returns the most recent `past_due` transaction.
* Where a subscription is `active`, it creates a new zero amount transaction for the items on a subscription.

You can use the returned `checkout.url`, or pass the returned transaction ID to Paddle.js to open a checkout to present customers with a way of updating their payment details.

The `customer`, `address`, `business`, `discount`, `adjustments` and `adjustments_totals` properties are only returned in the response if the API key has read permissions for those related entities.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/subscriptions/update-payment-method">Get a transaction to update payment method</a>

<h3 id="get-a-transaction-to-update-payment-method-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the subscription entity to work with.|

## Preview an update to a subscription

<a id="opIdpreview-subscription-update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/subscriptions/string/preview \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "items": [
      {
        "price_id": "pri_01gsz8x8sawmvhz1pv30nge1ke",
        "quantity": 20
      },
      {
        "price_id": "pri_01h1vjfevh5etwq3rb416a23h2",
        "quantity": 1
      },
      {
        "price_id": "pri_01gsz95g2zrkagg294kpstx54r",
        "quantity": 1
      }
    ],
    "proration_billing_mode": "prorated_immediately"
  }'
```

`PATCH /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/preview`

Previews an update for a subscription without applying those changes. Typically used for previewing proration before making changes to a subscription.

If successful, your response includes `immediate_transaction`, `next_transaction`, and `recurring_transaction_details` so you can see expected transactions for the changes.

The `update_summary` object contains details of prorated credits and charges created, along with the overall result of the update.

You can't preview updates for a subscription that's `past_due`, except to remove a scheduled change by setting `scheduled_change` to `null`.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/subscriptions/preview-subscription">Preview an update to a subscription</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "price_id": "pri_01gsz8x8sawmvhz1pv30nge1ke",
      "quantity": 20
    },
    {
      "price_id": "pri_01h1vjfevh5etwq3rb416a23h2",
      "quantity": 1
    },
    {
      "price_id": "pri_01gsz95g2zrkagg294kpstx54r",
      "quantity": 1
    }
  ],
  "proration_billing_mode": "prorated_immediately"
}
```

<h3 id="preview-an-update-to-a-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the subscription entity to work with.|
|body|body|[SubscriptionUpdate](#schemasubscriptionupdate)|true|none|
|» customer_id|body|object|false|Paddle ID of the customer that this subscription is for, prefixed with `ctm_`. Include to change the customer for a subscription.|
|» address_id|body|object|false|Paddle ID of the address that this subscription is for, prefixed with `add_`. Include to change the address for a subscription.|
|» business_id|body|[BusinessId](#schemabusinessid) \| null|false|Paddle ID of the business that this subscription is for, prefixed with `biz_`. Include to change the business for a subscription.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[BusinessId](#schemabusinessid)|false|Unique Paddle ID for this business entity, prefixed with `biz_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» currency_code|body|object|false|Supported three-letter ISO 4217 currency code. Include to change the currency that a subscription bills in. When changing `collection_mode` to `manual`, you may need to change currency code to `USD`, `EUR`, or `GBP`.|
|» next_billed_at|body|object|false|RFC 3339 datetime string of when this subscription is next scheduled to be billed. Include to change the next billing date.|
|» discount|body|[SubscriptionUpdateDiscount](#schemasubscriptionupdatediscount) \| null|false|Details of the discount applied to this subscription. Include to add a discount to a subscription. `null` to remove a discount.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[SubscriptionUpdateDiscount](#schemasubscriptionupdatediscount)|false|Details of the discount applied to this subscription. Include to add a discount to a subscription. `null` to remove a discount.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» collection_mode|body|object|false|How payment is collected for transactions created for this subscription. `automatic` for checkout, `manual` for invoices.|
|» billing_details|body|[BillingDetailsUpdate](#schemabillingdetailsupdate) \| null|false|Details for invoicing. Required if `collection_mode` is `manual`. `null` if changing `collection_mode` to `automatic`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[BillingDetailsUpdate](#schemabillingdetailsupdate)|false|Details for invoicing. Required if `collection_mode` is `manual`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» scheduled_change|body|null|false|Change that's scheduled to be applied to a subscription. When updating, you may only set to `null` to remove a scheduled change. Use the pause subscription, cancel subscription, and resume subscription operations to create scheduled changes.|
|» items|body|[[SubscriptionUpdateItems](#schemasubscriptionupdateitems)]|false|List of items on this subscription. Only recurring items may be added. Send the complete list of items that should be on this subscription, including existing items to retain.|
|» custom_data|body|[CustomData](#schemacustomdata) \| null|false|Your own structured key-value data.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[CustomData](#schemacustomdata)|false|Your own structured key-value data.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» proration_billing_mode|body|[SubscriptionUpdateProrationBillingMode](#schemasubscriptionupdateprorationbillingmode)|false|How Paddle should handle proration calculation for changes made to a subscription or its items. Required when making<br>changes that impact billing.<br><br>For automatically-collected subscriptions, responses may take longer than usual if a proration billing mode that<br>collects for payment immediately is used.|
|» on_payment_failure|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» proration_billing_mode|prorated_immediately|
|» proration_billing_mode|prorated_next_billing_period|
|» proration_billing_mode|full_immediately|
|» proration_billing_mode|full_next_billing_period|
|» proration_billing_mode|do_not_bill|

## Create a one-time charge for a subscription

<a id="opIdcreate-subscription-charge"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/subscriptions/string/charge \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "effective_from": "immediately",
    "items": [
      {
        "price_id": "pri_01gsz98e27ak2tyhexptwc58yk",
        "quantity": 1
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/charge`

Creates a new one-time charge for a subscription. Use to bill non-recurring items to a subscription. Non-recurring items are price entities where the `billing_cycle` is `null`.

You can't create one-time charges for subscriptions that are `past_due`.

If successful, Paddle responds with the updated subscription entity. However, one-time charges aren't held against the subscription entity, so the charges billed aren't returned in the response.

Once created, to get details of a one-time charge:

* When created with `effective_from` as `next_billing_period`, get the subscription the charge was billed to and use the `include` query parameter with the `next_transaction` value.
* When created with `effective_from` as `immediately`, list transactions and use the `subscription_id` query parameter with the subscription ID of the subscription the charge was billed to.

When an update results in an immediate charge, responses may take longer than usual while a payment attempt is processed.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/subscriptions/create-one-time-charge">Create a one-time charge for a subscription</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "effective_from": "immediately",
  "items": [
    {
      "price_id": "pri_01gsz98e27ak2tyhexptwc58yk",
      "quantity": 1
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-one-time-charge-for-a-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the subscription entity to work with.|
|body|body|[SubscriptionCharge](#schemasubscriptioncharge)|true|none|
|» effective_from|body|object|true|When one-time charges should be billed.|
|» items|body|[[SubscriptionChargeItems](#schemasubscriptionchargeitems)]|true|List of one-time charges to bill for. Only prices where the `billing_cycle` is `null` may be added.<br><br>You can charge for items that you've added to your catalog by passing the Paddle ID of an existing price entity, or you can charge for non-catalog items by passing a price object.<br><br>Non-catalog items can be for existing products, or you can pass a product object as part of your price to charge for a non-catalog product.|
|» on_payment_failure|body|object|false|none|

## Preview a one-time charge for a subscription

<a id="opIdpreview-subscription-charge"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/subscriptions/string/charge/preview \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "effective_from": "immediately",
    "items": [
      {
        "price_id": "pri_01gsz98e27ak2tyhexptwc58yk",
        "quantity": 1
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/charge/preview`

Previews creating a one-time charge for a subscription without billing that charge. Typically used for previewing calculations before making changes to a subscription.

One-time charges are non-recurring items. These are price entities where the `billing_cycle` is `null`.

You can't preview one-time charges for subscriptions that are `past_due`.

If successful, your response includes `immediate_transaction`, `next_transaction`, and `recurring_transaction_details` so you can see expected transactions for the changes.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/subscriptions/preview-subscription-charge">Preview a one-time charge for a subscription</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "effective_from": "immediately",
  "items": [
    {
      "price_id": "pri_01gsz98e27ak2tyhexptwc58yk",
      "quantity": 1
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="preview-a-one-time-charge-for-a-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the subscription entity to work with.|
|body|body|[SubscriptionCharge](#schemasubscriptioncharge)|true|none|
|» effective_from|body|object|true|When one-time charges should be billed.|
|» items|body|[[SubscriptionChargeItems](#schemasubscriptionchargeitems)]|true|List of one-time charges to bill for. Only prices where the `billing_cycle` is `null` may be added.<br><br>You can charge for items that you've added to your catalog by passing the Paddle ID of an existing price entity, or you can charge for non-catalog items by passing a price object.<br><br>Non-catalog items can be for existing products, or you can pass a product object as part of your price to charge for a non-catalog product.|
|» on_payment_failure|body|object|false|none|

<h1 id="paddle-api-subscription-history">Subscription history</h1>

Subscription history entries describe the changes made to a subscription over its lifetime, including what changed, when, and who made the change.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/subscription-history">Subscription history overview</a>

## List history for a subscription

<a id="opIdlist-subscription-history"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/subscriptions/sub_01h04vsc0qhwtsbsxh3422wjs4/history \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/history`

Returns a paginated list of history entries for a subscription. Use the query parameters to filter and page through results.

Subscription history records the changes made to a subscription over its lifetime, so you can see what changed, when it happened, where it originated, and who made the change. Each change is a separate history entry, and some entries also include a reason.

Paddle began recording subscription history on June 29, 2026. For subscriptions that existed before then, Paddle automatically creates `subscription_created` and `subscription_canceled` entries and attempts to infer details from the subscription's initial state.

History entries are ordered by newest first by default (`id` in descending order).

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/subscription-history/list-subscription-history">List history for a subscription</a>

<h3 id="list-history-for-a-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription_id|path|[SubscriptionId](#schemasubscriptionid)|true|none|
|action|query|[[SubscriptionHistoryActionQuery](#schemasubscriptionhistoryactionquery)]|false|Return history entries that match the specified action. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple action values.|
|source|query|[[SubscriptionHistorySourceQuery](#schemasubscriptionhistorysourcequery)]|false|Return history entries that match the specified source. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple source values.|
|actor_type|query|[[SubscriptionHistoryActorTypeQuery](#schemasubscriptionhistoryactortypequery)]|false|Return history entries that match the specified actor type. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple actor type values.|
|actor_id|query|[string]|false|Return history entries that match the specified actor ID. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple actor ID values. Only applicable if `actor_type` is also selected.|
|reason|query|[[SubscriptionHistoryReasonQuery](#schemasubscriptionhistoryreasonquery)]|false|Return history entries that match the specified reason. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple reason values.|
|occurred_at|query|string|false|Return entities that occurred at a specific time. Use `[LTE]` (less than or equal to) or `[GTE]` (greater than or equal to) operators with an RFC 3339 datetime string. For example, `occurred_at[LTE]=2023-04-18T17:03:26` or `occurred_at[GTE]=2023-04-18T17:03:26`.|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `50`; Maximum: `200`.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Order returned entities by the specified field and direction (`[ASC]` or `[DESC]`). For example, `?order_by=id[DESC]`.<br><br>Valid fields for ordering: `id`.|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

<h1 id="paddle-api-simulations">Simulations</h1>

Simulation entities describe a reusable configuration for testing webhooks.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/simulations">Simulations entity overview</a>

## List simulations

<a id="opIdlist-simulations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/simulations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /simulations`

Returns a paginated list of simulations. Use the query parameters to [page through results](https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/about/pagination).

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/simulations/list-simulations">List simulations</a>

<h3 id="list-simulations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|query|[string]|false|Return only the IDs specified. Use a comma-separated list to get multiple entities.|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `50`; Maximum: `200`.|
|notification_setting_id|query|[string]|false|Return entities related to the specified notification destination. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple notification destination IDs.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Order returned entities by the specified field and direction (`[ASC]` or `[DESC]`). For example, `?order_by=id[ASC]`.<br><br>Valid fields for ordering: `id`.|
|status|query|[[StatusQuery](#schemastatusquery)]|false|Return entities that match the specified status. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple status values.|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|archived|

## Create a simulation

<a id="opIdcreate-simulation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/simulations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "notification_setting_id": "ntfset_01j82d983j814ypzx7m1fw2jpz",
    "name": "Create a failed subscription renewal simulation with subscription ID",
    "type": "subscription_renewal",
    "config": {
      "subscription_renewal": {
        "entities": {
          "subscription_id": "sub_01h04vsc0qhwtsbsxh3422wjs4"
        },
        "options": {
          "payment_outcome": "failed",
          "dunning_exhausted_action": "subscription_canceled"
        }
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /simulations`

Creates a new simulation for a notification setting (notification destination).

simulated webhook payloads with real data. The API key making the request needs read permissions:

* For the entities you provided, or the request fails.
* For related entities which aren't nested in the entities you provided, or static examples will be used instead.

For example, when creating a subscription renewal scenario simulation with an API key that has a `subscription.read` permission but not a `transaction.read` permission,
the request succeeds and the subscription data will be used in simulated payloads, but the related transaction data won't be used in payloads and falls back to a static example.

If you don't provide a `config.entities` object, simulated webhook payloads are populated with static examples.

If successful, your response includes a copy of the new simulation entity.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/simulations/create-simulation">Create a simulation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "notification_setting_id": "ntfset_01j82d983j814ypzx7m1fw2jpz",
  "name": "Create a failed subscription renewal simulation with subscription ID",
  "type": "subscription_renewal",
  "config": {
    "subscription_renewal": {
      "entities": {
        "subscription_id": "sub_01h04vsc0qhwtsbsxh3422wjs4"
      },
      "options": {
        "payment_outcome": "failed",
        "dunning_exhausted_action": "subscription_canceled"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`PATCH /simulations/{simulation_id}`

Updates a simulation using its ID.

For scenario simulations, you can optionally include a `config.entities` object in the request body with entity IDs to populate
simulated webhook payloads with real data. The API key making the request needs read permissions:

* For the entities you provided, or the request fails.
* For related entities which aren't nested in the entities you provided, or static examples will be used instead.

For example, when updating a subscription renewal scenario simulation with an API key that has a `subscription.read` permission but not a `transaction.read` permission,
the request succeeds and the subscription data will be used in simulated payloads, but the related transaction data won't be used in payloads and falls back to a static example.

If you don't provide a `config.entities` object, simulated webhook payloads are populated with static examples.

If successful, your response includes a copy of the updated simulation entity.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/simulations/update-simulation">Update a simulation</a>

<h1 id="paddle-api-simulation-runs">Simulation runs</h1>

Simulation run entities describe an attempt by Paddle to send simulated events for a notification simulation.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/simulation-runs">Simulation runs entity overview</a>

## List runs for a simulation

<a id="opIdlist-simulation-runs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/simulations/string/runs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /simulations/{simulation_id}/runs`

Returns a paginated list of simulation runs. Use the query parameters to [page through results](https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/about/pagination).

Use the `include` parameter to [include related entities](https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/about/include-entities) in the response.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/simulation-runs/list-simulation-runs">List runs for a simulation</a>

<h3 id="list-runs-for-a-simulation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|simulation_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the simulation entity to work with.|
|id|query|[string]|false|Return only the IDs specified. Use a comma-separated list to get multiple entities.|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `50`; Maximum: `200`.|
|include|query|[[SimulationsRunIncludeEnum](#schemasimulationsrunincludeenum)]|false|Include related entities in the response.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Order returned entities by the specified field and direction (`[ASC]` or `[DESC]`). For example, `?order_by=id[ASC]`.<br><br>Valid fields for ordering: `id`.|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|include|events|

## Create a run for a simulation

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"

<h1 id="paddle-api-simulation-run-events">Simulation run events</h1>

Simulation run event entities describe a simulated event that happened as part of a notification simulation run.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/simulation-run-events">Simulation run events entity overview</a>

## List events for a simulation run

<a id="opIdlist-simulations-events"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/simulations/string/runs/string/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /simulations/{simulation_id}/runs/{simulation_run_id}/events`

Returns a paginated list of simulations. Use the query parameters to [page through results](https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/about/pagination).

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/simulation-events/list-simulation-events">List events for a simulation run</a>

<h3 id="list-events-for-a-simulation-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|simulation_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the simulation entity to work with.|
|simulation_run_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the simulation run entity to work with.|
|id|query|[string]|false|Return only the IDs specified. Use a comma-separated list to get multiple entities.|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `50`; Maximum: `200`.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Order returned entities by the specified field and direction (`[ASC]` or `[DESC]`). For example, `?order_by=id[ASC]`.<br><br>Valid fields for ordering: `id`.|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

## Replay an event for a simulation run

<a id="opIdreplay-simulation-run-event"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/simulations/string/runs/string/events/string/replay \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /simulations/{simulation_id}/runs/{simulation_run_id}/events/{simulation_event_id}/replay`

Attempts to resend a simulation run log using its ID.

Paddle creates a new simulation run log entity for the replay, related to the same simulation run.

If successful, your response includes the new simulation run log entity.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/simulation-events/replay-simulation-run-event">Replay an event for a simulation run</a>

<h3 id="replay-an-event-for-a-simulation-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|simulation_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the simulation entity to work with.|
|simulation_run_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the simulation run entity to work with.|
|simulation_event_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the simulation event entity to work with.|
