<h1 id="paddle-api-settings">Settings</h1>

Settings entities describe how your account is configured, including checkout, sales tax, currency, and statement descriptor settings. There's one of each for your account, so you get and update them without an ID.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/settings">Settings overview</a>

## Get balance currency settings

<a id="opIdget-balance-currency"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/settings/balance-currency \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /settings/balance-currency`

Returns the balance currency settings for your account.

Includes the currency that your Paddle balance is held in and paid out from (`primary`), the currency that you'd like it to be held in instead (`preferred`), and the currencies enabled for your account (`enabled`).

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/settings/get-balance-currency">Get balance currency settings</a>

## Update balance currency settings

<a id="opIdupdate-balance-currency"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/settings/balance-currency \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "preferred": "GBP"
  }'
```

`PATCH /settings/balance-currency`

Updates the balance currency settings for your account.

You can only change `preferred`. Paddle then updates `primary` to match, but when depends on your account.

If more than one currency is in `enabled`, Paddle updates `primary` immediately. `preferred` must be one of the currencies in `enabled`, otherwise the request returns an `invalid_field` error.

Otherwise, Paddle updates `primary` when your balance is zero. That's immediately if it's already zero, or after your next payout if it isn't. Until then, `primary` and `preferred` are different.

If successful, your response includes a copy of the updated balance currency settings entity.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/settings/update-balance-currency">Update balance currency settings</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "preferred": "GBP"
}
```

<h3 id="update-balance-currency-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BalanceCurrencyUpdate](#schemabalancecurrencyupdate)|true|none|
|» preferred|body|object|false|Currency that you'd like your Paddle balance to be held in and paid out from. If more than one currency is in `enabled`, it must be one of them.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "primary": "USD",
    "preferred": "GBP",
    "enabled": [
      "USD"
    ]
  },
  "meta": {
    "request_id": "9bcdcc29-e180-4055-ad3d-d37e5dc5e56d"
  }
}
```

## Update checkout payment method settings

<a id="opIdupdate-checkout-payment-method-settings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/settings/checkout-payment-methods \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "payment_methods": {
      "apple_pay": {
        "enabled": true
      },
      "alipay": {
        "enabled": false
      }
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /settings/checkout-payment-methods`

Updates the checkout payment method settings for your account.

Send only the payment methods that you want to change. Payment methods that you omit keep their current value. Paddle sets `available`, so you can't update it.

Returns a `checkout_payment_method_not_available` error if you enable a payment method that isn't available on your account, and a `checkout_payment_method_unknown` error if the request includes a payment method that Paddle doesn't recognize.

If successful, your response includes a copy of the updated checkout payment method settings entity.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/settings/update-checkout-payment-method-settings">Update checkout payment method settings</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "payment_methods": {
    "apple_pay": {
      "enabled": true
    },
    "alipay": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CheckoutPaymentMethodSettingsUpdate](#schemacheckoutpaymentmethodsettingsupdate)|true|none|
|» payment_methods|body|object|true|Settings to update for each payment method, keyed by payment method. Send only the payment methods that you want to change.|

## Update checkout URL settings

<a id="opIdupdate-checkout-url"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/settings/checkout-url \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "default_url": "https://example.com/checkout"
  }'
```

`PATCH /settings/checkout-url`

Updates the checkout URL settings for your account.

Pass `null` to clear `default_url`.

In live accounts, the URL's domain must be an approved checkout domain for your account, or the request returns a `checkout_url_domain_not_approved` error. Sandbox accounts accept any `https` URL.

If successful, your response includes a copy of the updated checkout URL settings entity.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/settings/update-checkout-url">Update checkout URL settings</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "default_url": "https://example.com/checkout"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CheckoutUrlUpdate](#schemacheckouturlupdate)|true|none|
|» default_url|body|string \| null(uri)|false|URL that Paddle opens when a checkout is created without a URL of its own. Pass `null` to clear it.<br><br>Must use `https`. In live accounts, its domain must also be an approved checkout domain for your account.<br><br>Paddle appends `?_ptxn=` and the transaction ID to this URL. The page must have Paddle.js set up to read it and open the checkout.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

## Get currency conversion settings

<a id="opIdget-currency-conversions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/settings/currency-conversions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /settings/currency-conversions`

Returns the currency conversion settings for your account.

When a currency is enabled, Paddle automatically converts prices into it at checkout for customers whose local currency it is. A price override for the customer's country takes precedence over the converted price. When a currency isn't enabled, those customers see the price in its base currency instead. These settings don't limit which currencies you can use for prices or price overrides.

The response is keyed by currency code and includes every supported currency, whether or not you've changed it. It isn't paginated.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/settings/get-currency-conversions">Get currency conversion settings</a>

## Update statement descriptor settings

<a id="opIdupdate-statement-descriptor-settings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/settings/statement-descriptor \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "AEROEDIT"
  }'
```

`PATCH /settings/statement-descriptor`

Updates the statement descriptor settings for your account.

Paddle sets `preview` based on `name`, so you can't update it directly.

Returns a `statement_descriptor_invalid_name` error if the supplied name doesn't meet the format requirements, a `statement_descriptor_in_use` error if the supplied name is already in use, and a `statement_descriptor_not_found` error if no statement descriptor exists for your account yet.

If successful, your response includes a copy of the updated statement descriptor settings entity.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/settings/update-statement-descriptor-settings">Update statement descriptor settings</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "AEROEDIT"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[StatementDescriptorSettingsUpdate](#schemastatementdescriptorsettingsupdate)|true|none|
|» name|body|[StatementDescriptorName](#schemastatementdescriptorname)|false|Name that appears on the customer's bank or card statement. 2-10 characters. May contain uppercase letters, digits, spaces, and dots; must contain at least one letter; dots can't be the first or last character.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
    "name": "AEROEDIT",
```

<h1 id="paddle-api-reports">Reports</h1>

Report entities describe a report generated in your Paddle system.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/reports">Reports entity overview</a>

## List reports

<a id="opIdlist-reports"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/reports \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /reports`

Returns a paginated list of reports. Use the query parameters to page through results.

By default, Paddle returns reports that are `pending` or `ready`. Use the `status` query parameter to return reports that are `failed`, `expired`, or `deleted`.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/reports/list-reports">List reports</a>

<h3 id="list-reports-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `50`; Maximum: `200`.|

|status|query|[[ReportStatusQueryEnum](#schemareportstatusqueryenum)]|false|Return entities that match the specified status. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple status values.|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

## Create a report

<a id="opIdcreate-report"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/reports \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "transactions",
    "filters": [
      {
        "name": "collection_mode",
        "value": [
          "manual"
        ]
      },
      {
        "name": "updated_at",
        "value": "2024-04-15",
        "operator": "lt"
      },
      {
        "name": "updated_at",
        "value": "2024-01-01",
        "operator": "gte"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /reports`

Creates a new report.

Reports are created as `pending` initially while Paddle generates your report. They move to `ready` when they're ready to download.

You can download a report when it's ready using the [get a CSV file for a report operation](https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/reports/get-report-csv).

If successful, your response includes a copy of the new report entity.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/reports/create-report">Create a report</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "transactions",
  "filters": [
    {
      "name": "collection_mode",
      "value": [
        "manual"
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "updated_at",
      "value": "2024-04-15",
      "operator": "lt"
    },
    {
      "name": "updated_at",
      "value": "2024-01-01",
      "operator": "gte"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ReportCreate](#schemareportcreate)|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[ReportAdjustmentsCreateModel](#schemareportadjustmentscreatemodel)|false|Entity when working with reports for adjustments or adjustment line items.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[ReportTransactionsCreateModel](#schemareporttransactionscreatemodel)|false|Entity when working with reports for transaction or transaction line items.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[ReportProductsPricesCreateModel](#schemareportproductspricescreatemodel)|false|Entity when working with a products and prices report.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[ReportDiscountsCreateModel](#schemareportdiscountscreatemodel)|false|Entity when working with a discounts report.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[ReportBalanceCreateModel](#schemareportbalancecreatemodel)|false|**Deprecated.** Entity when working with a balance report. Deprecated.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[ReportPayoutReconciliationCreateModel](#schemareportpayoutreconciliationcreatemodel)|false|Entity when working with a reconciliation report.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[ReportCheckoutsCreateModel](#schemareportcheckoutscreatemodel)|false|Entity when working with a checkouts report.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[ReportSubscriptionsCreateModel](#schemareportsubscriptionscreatemodel)|false|Entity when working with a subscriptions report.|

## Get a CSV file for a report

<a id="opIdget-report-csv"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/reports/string/download-url \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /reports/{report_id}/download-url`

Returns a link to a CSV file for a report.

Only returned for reports that are `ready`. This means Paddle has completed processing the report and it's ready to download.

The link returned is not a permanent link. It expires after 3 minutes.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/reports/get-report-csv">Get a CSV file for a report</a>

<h3 id="get-a-csv-file-for-a-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

<h1 id="paddle-api-products">Products</h1>

Product entities describe the items that customers can purchase. They hold high-level product attributes.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/products">Product entity overview</a>

## List products

<a id="opIdlist-products"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/products \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /products`

Returns a paginated list of products. Use the query parameters to page through results.

By default, Paddle returns products that are `active`. Use the `status` query parameter to return products that are archived.

Use the `include` parameter to include related price entities in the response.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/products/list-products">List products</a>

<h3 id="list-products-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|query|[string]|false|Return only the IDs specified. Use a comma-separated list to get multiple entities.|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `50`; Maximum: `200`.|
|include|query|[[ProductIncludeEnum](#schemaproductincludeenum)]|false|Include related entities in the response. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple entities.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Order returned entities by the specified field and direction (`[ASC]` or `[DESC]`). For example, `?order_by=id[ASC]`.<br><br>Valid fields for ordering: `created_at`, `custom_data`, `description`, `id`, `image_url`, `name`, `status`, `tax_category`, and `updated_at`.|
|status|query|[[StatusQuery](#schemastatusquery)]|false|Return entities that match the specified status. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple status values.|
|tax_category|query|[[TaxCategoryQueryEnum](#schemataxcategoryqueryenum)]|false|Return entities that match the specified tax category. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple tax categories.|
|type|query|[CatalogTypeQueryEnum](#schemacatalogtypequeryenum)|false|Return items that match the specified type.|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|include|prices|
|status|active|
|status|archived|
|tax_category|digital-goods|
|tax_category|ebooks|
|tax_category|implementation-services|
|tax_category|professional-services|
|tax_category|saas|
|tax_category|software-programming-services|
|tax_category|standard|
|tax_category|training-services|
|tax_category|website-hosting|
|type|custom|
|type|standard|

<h1 id="paddle-api-pricing-preview">Pricing preview</h1>

Pricing previews are calculated totals for prices.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/pricing-preview">Pricing preview overview</a>

## Preview prices

<a id="opIdpreview-prices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/pricing-preview \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "items": [
      {
        "quantity": 20,
        "price_id": "pri_01gsz8z1q1n00f12qt82y31smh"
      },
      {
        "quantity": 1,
        "price_id": "pri_01h1vjfevh5etwq3rb416a23h2"
      }
    ],
    "currency_code": "USD",
    "discount_id": "dsc_01gtgztp8fpchantd5g1wrksa3",
    "customer_ip_address": "34.232.58.13"
  }'
```

`POST /pricing-preview`

Previews calculations for one or more prices. Typically used for building pricing pages.

You can provide location information when previewing prices. You must provide this if you want Paddle to calculate tax or [automatically localize prices](https://developer.paddle.com/build/products/offer-localized-pricing). You can provide one of:

* `customer_ip_address`: Paddle fetches location using the IP address to calculate totals.
* `address`: Paddle uses the country and ZIP code (where supplied) to calculate totals.
* `customer_id`, `address_id`, `business_id`: Paddle uses existing customer data to calculate totals. Typically used for logged-in customers.

If successful, your response includes the data you sent with a `details` object that includes totals for the supplied prices.

Each line item includes `formatted_unit_totals` and `formatted_totals` objects that return totals formatted for the country or region you're working with, including the currency symbol.

You can work with the preview prices operation using the [`Paddle.PricePreview()`](https://developer.paddle.com/paddlejs/methods/paddle-pricepreview) method in Paddle.js. When working with `Paddle.PricePreview()`, request and response fields are `camelCase` rather than `snake_case`.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/pricing-preview/preview-prices">Preview prices</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "quantity": 20,
      "price_id": "pri_01gsz8z1q1n00f12qt82y31smh"
    },
    {
      "quantity": 1,
      "price_id": "pri_01h1vjfevh5etwq3rb416a23h2"
    }
  ],
  "currency_code": "USD",
  "discount_id": "dsc_01gtgztp8fpchantd5g1wrksa3",
  "customer_ip_address": "34.232.58.13"
}
```

<h3 id="preview-prices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TransactionPricingPreviewRequest](#schematransactionpricingpreviewrequest)|true|none|
|» customer_id|body|[CustomerId](#schemacustomerid) \| null|false|Paddle ID of the customer that this preview is for, prefixed with `ctm_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[CustomerId](#schemacustomerid)|false|Unique Paddle ID for this customer entity, prefixed with `ctm_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» address_id|body|[AddressId](#schemaaddressid) \| null|false|Paddle ID of the address that this preview is for, prefixed with `add_`. Send one of `address_id`, `customer_ip_address`, or the `address` object when previewing.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[AddressId](#schemaaddressid)|false|Unique Paddle ID for this address entity, prefixed with `add_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» business_id|body|[BusinessId](#schemabusinessid) \| null|false|Paddle ID of the business that this preview is for, prefixed with `biz_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[BusinessId](#schemabusinessid)|false|Unique Paddle ID for this business entity, prefixed with `biz_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» currency_code|body|[CurrencyCode](#schemacurrencycode) \| null|false|Supported three-letter ISO 4217 currency code.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[CurrencyCode](#schemacurrencycode)|false|Supported three-letter ISO 4217 currency code.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» discount_id|body|[DiscountId](#schemadiscountid) \| null|false|Paddle ID of the discount applied to this preview, prefixed with `dsc_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[DiscountId](#schemadiscountid)|false|Unique Paddle ID for this discount, prefixed with `dsc_`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» address|body|[AddressPreviewCreate](#schemaaddresspreviewcreate) \| null|false|Address for this preview. Send one of `address_id`, `customer_ip_address`, or the `address` object when previewing.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[AddressPreviewCreate](#schemaaddresspreviewcreate)|false|Represents an address entity when previewing addresses.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

<h1 id="paddle-api-prices">Prices</h1>

Price entities describe how much and how often you charge for your products. They hold charging information.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/prices">Price entity overview</a>

## List prices

<a id="opIdlist-prices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/prices \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /prices`

Returns a paginated list of prices. Use the query parameters to page through results.

By default, Paddle returns prices that are `active`. Use the `status` query parameter to return prices that are archived.

Use the `include` parameter to include the related product entity in the response.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/prices/list-prices">List prices</a>

<h3 id="list-prices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|query|[string]|false|Return only the IDs specified. Use a comma-separated list to get multiple entities.|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `50`; Maximum: `200`.|
|include|query|[[PriceListIncludeEnum](#schemapricelistincludeenum)]|false|Include related entities in the response.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Order returned entities by the specified field and direction (`[ASC]` or `[DESC]`). For example, `?order_by=id[ASC]`.<br><br>Valid fields for ordering: `billing_cycle.frequency`, `billing_cycle.interval`, `id`, `product_id`, `quantity.maximum`, `quantity.minimum`, `status`, `tax_mode`, `unit_price.amount`, and `unit_price.currency_code`.|
|product_id|query|[string]|false|Return entities related to the specified product. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple product IDs.|
|status|query|[[StatusQuery](#schemastatusquery)]|false|Return entities that match the specified status. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple status values.|
|recurring|query|boolean|false|Determine whether returned entities are for recurring prices (`true`) or one-time prices (`false`).|
|billing_cycle.interval|query|[DurationInterval](#schemadurationinterval)|false|Return entities where the price billing cycle interval matches this value.|
|billing_cycle.frequency|query|integer|false|Return entities where the price billing cycle frequency matches this value.|
|type|query|[CatalogTypeQueryEnum](#schemacatalogtypequeryenum)|false|Return items that match the specified type.|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|include|product|
|status|active|
|status|archived|
|billing_cycle.interval|day|
|billing_cycle.interval|week|
|billing_cycle.interval|month|
|billing_cycle.interval|year|
|type|custom|
|type|standard|

## Create a price

<a id="opIdcreate-price"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/prices \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Monthly (per seat) with 14 day paid trial",
    "name": "Monthly (per seat)",
    "product_id": "pro_01htz88xpr0mm7b3ta2pjkr7w2",
    "unit_price": {
      "amount": "500",
      "currency_code": "USD"
    },
    "billing_cycle": {
      "interval": "month",
      "frequency": 1
    },
    "trial_period": {
      "interval": "day",
      "frequency": 14,
      "requires_payment_method": true,
      "unit_price": {
        "amount": "100",
        "currency_code": "USD"
      }
    },
    "tax_mode": "account_setting"
  }'
```

`POST /prices`

Creates a new price.

Prices describe how you charge for products. You must include a `product_id` in your request to relate this price to a product.

If you omit the `quantity` object, Paddle automatically sets a minimum of `1` and a maximum of `100` for you. This means the most units that a customer can buy is 100. Set a quantity if you'd like to offer a different amount.

If successful, your response includes a copy of the new price entity.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/prices/create-price">Create a price</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Monthly (per seat) with 14 day paid trial",
  "name": "Monthly (per seat)",
  "product_id": "pro_01htz88xpr0mm7b3ta2pjkr7w2",
  "unit_price": {
    "amount": "500",
    "currency_code": "USD"
  },
  "billing_cycle": {
    "interval": "month",
    "frequency": 1
  },
  "trial_period": {
    "interval": "day",
    "frequency": 14,
    "requires_payment_method": true,
    "unit_price": {
      "amount": "100",
      "currency_code": "USD"
    }
  },
  "tax_mode": "account_setting"
}
```

<h1 id="paddle-api-payment-methods">Payment methods</h1>

Payment method entities hold information about a payment method a customer saved at checkout for use in the future. They're related to customer entities.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/payment-methods">Payment methods entity overview</a>

## List payment methods for a customer

<a id="opIdlist-customer-payment-methods"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/customers/ctm_01grnn4zta5a1mf02jjze7y2ys/payment-methods \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /customers/{customer_id}/payment-methods`

Returns a paginated list of payment methods that a customer has saved.  Use the query parameters to page through results.

Customers can choose to save payment methods when purchasing one-time items and subscriptions by checking a box when completing checkout. You can present customers with their saved payment methods when they make a purchase in the future.

Returns an empty list where customers have not saved any payment methods, or have deleted all previously saved payment methods.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/payment-methods/list-payment-methods">List payment methods for a customer</a>

<h3 id="list-payment-methods-for-a-customer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer_id|path|[CustomerId](#schemacustomerid)|true|Paddle ID of the customer entity to work with.|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `50`; Maximum: `200`.|
|address_id|query|[string]|false|Return entities related to the specified address. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple address IDs.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Order returned entities by the specified field and direction (`[ASC]` or `[DESC]`). For example, `?order_by=id[ASC]`.<br><br>Valid fields for ordering: `id`.|
|supports_checkout|query|boolean|false|Return entities that support being presented at checkout (`true`) or not (`false`).|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

## Delete a payment method for a customer

<a id="opIddelete-customer-payment-method"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/customers/ctm_01grnn4zta5a1mf02jjze7y2ys/payment-methods/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /customers/{customer_id}/payment-methods/{payment_method_id}`

Deletes a customer payment method using its ID.

Deleted payment methods are no longer saved and presented to the customer for future purchases.

Saved payment methods can't be deleted if tied to an `active`, `trialing`, `paused`, or `past_due` subscription. Update the subscription's payment method first, then delete the saved payment method.

There's no way to recover a deleted saved payment method. It's permanently removed from that customer.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/payment-methods/delete-payment-method">Delete a payment method for a customer</a>

<h3 id="delete-a-payment-method-for-a-customer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer_id|path|[CustomerId](#schemacustomerid)|true|Paddle ID of the customer entity to work with.|
|payment_method_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the payment method entity to work with.|

> Example responses

<h1 id="paddle-api-notifications">Notifications</h1>

Notification entities describe a notification for an event that happened in your Paddle system.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/notifications">Notification entity overview</a>

## List notifications

<a id="opIdlist-notifications"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/notifications \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /notifications`

Returns a paginated list of notifications created in the last 90 days. Use the query parameters to page through results.

Notifications older than 90 days aren't retained.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/notifications/list-notifications">List notifications</a>

<h3 id="list-notifications-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `50`; Maximum: `200`.|
|notification_setting_id|query|[string]|false|Return entities related to the specified notification destination. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple notification destination IDs.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Order returned entities by the specified field and direction (`[ASC]` or `[DESC]`). For example, `?order_by=id[ASC]`.<br><br>Valid fields for ordering: `id`.|
|search|query|string|false|Return entities that match a search query. Searches `id` and `type` fields.|
|status|query|[[NotificationStatusQueryEnum](#schemanotificationstatusqueryenum)]|false|Return entities that match the specified status. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple status values.|
|filter|query|string|false|Return entities that contain the value specified. Pass a Paddle ID or email address that appears in the event payload, or part of one. Complete Paddle IDs and email addresses match exactly; partial values match as a prefix or substring, and must be at least three characters.|
|to|query|string|false|Return entities up to a specific time. Pass an RFC 3339 datetime string.|
|from|query|string|false|Return entities from a specific time. Pass an RFC 3339 datetime string.|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|delivered|
|status|failed|
|status|needs_retry|
|status|not_attempted|

## Get a notification

<a id="opIdget-notification"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/notifications/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /notifications/{notification_id}`

Returns a notification using its ID.

Notifications older than 90 days aren't retained. If you try to get a notification that's no longer retained, Paddle returns an error.

## Replay a notification

<a id="opIdreplay-notification"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/notifications/string/replay \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /notifications/{notification_id}/replay`

Attempts to resend a `delivered` or `failed` notification using its ID.

Paddle creates a new notification entity for the replay, related to the same `event_id`. Your response includes the new `notification_id` of the created notification.

Notifications older than 90 days aren't retained. If you try to replay a notification that's no longer retained, Paddle returns an error.

Only notifications with the `origin` of `event` can be replayed. You can't replay a notification created for a replay.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/notifications/replay-notification">Replay a notification</a>

<h3 id="replay-a-notification-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|notification_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the notification entity to work with.|

<h1 id="paddle-api-notification-settings">Notification settings</h1>

Notification settings entities describe subscriptions to events. They're also called notification destinations.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/notification-settings">Notification settings entity overview</a>

## List notification settings

<a id="opIdlist-notification-settings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/notification-settings \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /notification-settings`

Returns a paginated list of notification settings (notification destinations).

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/notification-settings/list-notification-settings">List notification settings</a>

<h3 id="list-notification-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `200`; Maximum: `200`.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Order returned entities by the specified field and direction (`[ASC]` or `[DESC]`). For example, `?order_by=id[ASC]`.<br><br>Valid fields for ordering: `id`.|
|active|query|boolean|false|Determine whether returned entities are active (`true`) or not (`false`).|
|traffic_source|query|[NotificationSettingTrafficSource](#schemanotificationsettingtrafficsource)|false|Return entities that match the specified traffic source.|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|traffic_source|platform|
|traffic_source|simulation|
|traffic_source|all|

## Create a notification setting

<a id="opIdcreate-notification-setting"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/notification-settings \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Slack notifications",
    "type": "url",
    "destination": "https://hooks.slack.com/example",
    "api_version": 1,
    "traffic_source": "all",
    "subscribed_events": [
      "transaction.billed",
      "transaction.canceled",
      "transaction.completed",
      "transaction.created",
      "transaction.payment_failed",
      "transaction.ready",
      "transaction.updated",
      "subscription.activated",
      "subscription.created",
      "subscription.past_due",
      "subscription.paused",
      "subscription.resumed",
      "subscription.trialing",
      "subscription.updated"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /notification-settings`

Creates a new notification setting (notification destination).

Pass an array of event type names to `subscribed_events` to say which events you'd like to subscribe to. Paddle responds with the full event type object for each event type.

If successful, your response includes a copy of the new notification setting entity. Use the returned `endpoint_secret_key` for webhook signature verification.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/notification-settings/create-notification-setting">Create a notification setting</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Slack notifications",
  "type": "url",
  "destination": "https://hooks.slack.com/example",
  "api_version": 1,
  "traffic_source": "all",
  "subscribed_events": [
    "transaction.billed",
    "transaction.canceled",
    "transaction.completed",
    "transaction.created",
    "transaction.payment_failed",
    "transaction.ready",
    "transaction.updated",
    "subscription.activated",
```

## Delete a notification setting

<a id="opIddelete-notification-setting"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/notification-settings/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /notification-settings/{notification_setting_id}`

Deletes a notification setting (notification destination) using its ID.

When you delete a notification setting, it's permanently removed from your account. Paddle stops sending events to your destination, and you'll lose access to all the logs for this notification setting.

There's no way to recover a deleted notification setting. Deactivate a notification setting using the update notification setting operation if you'll need access to the logs or want to reactivate later on.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/notification-settings/delete-notification-setting">Delete a notification setting</a>

<h3 id="delete-a-notification-setting-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|notification_setting_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the notification setting entity (notification destination) to work with.|

## Update a notification setting

<a id="opIdupdate-notification-setting"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/notification-settings/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Slack notifications (old)",
    "active": false
  }'
```

`PATCH /notification-settings/{notification_setting_id}`

Updates a notification setting (notification destination) using its ID.

When updating subscribed events, send the complete list of event types that you'd like to subscribe to — including existing event types. If you omit event types, they're removed from the notification setting.

You only need to pass an event type name. Paddle responds with the full event type object for each event type.

If successful, your response includes a copy of the updated notification setting entity.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/notification-settings/update-notification-setting">Update a notification setting</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Slack notifications (old)",
  "active": false
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-notification-setting-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|notification_setting_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the notification setting entity (notification destination) to work with.|
|body|body|[NotificationSettingUpdate](#schemanotificationsettingupdate)|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|Short description for this notification destination. Shown in the Paddle Dashboard.|
|» destination|body|string|false|Webhook endpoint URL or email address.|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Whether Paddle should try to deliver events to this notification destination.|
|» api_version|body|integer|false|API version that returned objects for events should conform to. Must be a valid version of the Paddle API. Can't be a version older than your account default. Defaults to your account default if omitted.|
|» include_sensitive_fields|body|boolean|false|Whether potentially sensitive fields should be sent to this notification destination.|
|» subscribed_events|body|[[EventTypeName](#schemaeventtypename)]|false|Subscribed events for this notification destination. When creating or updating a notification destination, pass an array of event type names only. Paddle returns the complete event type object.|
|» traffic_source|body|object|false|Whether Paddle should deliver real platform events, simulation events or both to this notification destination.|

<h1 id="paddle-api-notification-logs">Notification logs</h1>

Notification logs are records of an attempt to deliver a notification.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/notification-logs">Notification logs entity overview</a>

## List logs for a notification

<a id="opIdlist-notification-logs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/notifications/string/logs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /notifications/{notification_id}/logs`

Returns a paginated list of notification logs for a notification. A log includes information about delivery attempts, including failures.

Notifications older than 90 days aren't retained. If you try to list logs for a notification that's no longer retained, Paddle returns an error.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/notification-logs/list-notification-logs">List logs for a notification</a>

<h3 id="list-logs-for-a-notification-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `50`; Maximum: `200`.|
|notification_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the notification entity to work with.|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

<h1 id="paddle-api-metrics">Metrics</h1>

Metrics entities contain timeseries data about your Paddle account, including revenue, subscribers, and conversions.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/metrics">Metrics overview</a>

## List Explore metric entities

<a id="opIdlist-explore-metric-entities"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/metrics/explore/entities \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /metrics/explore/entities`

Returns a list of queryable Explore metrics and their related metadata, including time dimension, the dimensions you can group by, and measures with their allowed aggregations.

`subscriptions` isn't available in sandbox, where it's treated as `unknown_entity`.

By default, Paddle returns all metrics that are available. Use the `entity` query parameter to return a single one.

The response is not paginated.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/metrics/list-explore-metric-entities">List Explore metric entities</a>

<h3 id="list-explore-metric-entities-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|entity|query|[MetricEntity](#schemametricentity)|false|Return the metric that matches the specified entity name. Omit to return all metrics that are available. An unknown value, including `subscriptions` in sandbox, returns `unknown_entity`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|entity|transactions.completed|
|entity|adjustments.refunds|
|entity|adjustments.chargebacks|
|entity|checkouts|
|entity|subscriptions|

## Run an Explore metrics query

<a id="opIdrun-explore-metrics-query"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/metrics/explore \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "entity": "transactions.completed",
    "from": "2026-05-01",
    "to": "2026-08-01",
    "interval": "month",
    "dimensions": [
      "product"
    ],
    "measures": [
      {
        "field": "gross_revenue",
        "agg": "sum"
      }
    ],
    "order_by": [
      {
        "field": "gross_revenue",
        "dir": "desc"
      }
    ],
    "per_page": 5
  }'
```

`POST /metrics/explore`

Runs a query against a single Explore metric and returns timeseries data for it.

Pass the `entity` you want to query, a date range using `from` and `to`, an `interval`, and one or more `measures`. Include `dimensions` to break results down, `filters` to narrow them, and `order_by` to control which results are returned first.

Use the [list Explore metric entities](https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/metrics/list-explore-metric-entities) operation to see the dimensions, measures, and filters available for a metric.

Results are broken down into segments, where a segment is one combination of the dimensions you grouped by. `per_page` limits the number of segments returned, not the number of datapoints. A page can hold up to 10,000 datapoints, calculated as `per_page` multiplied by the number of time buckets in your range. Requests over this limit return `too_many_datapoints`.

If successful, your response includes the query results in `data`, with a self-describing `fields` block and one entry in `series` for each segment.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/metrics/run-explore-metrics-query">Run an Explore metrics query</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "entity": "transactions.completed",
  "from": "2026-05-01",
  "to": "2026-08-01",
  "interval": "month",
  "dimensions": [
    "product"
  ],
  "measures": [
    {
      "field": "gross_revenue",
      "agg": "sum"
    }
  ],
  "order_by": [
    {
      "field": "gross_revenue",
      "dir": "desc"
    }
  ],
  "per_page": 5
}
```

<h3 id="run-an-explore-metrics-query-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after|query|[MetricsExploreCursor](#schemametricsexplorecursor)|false|Pagination cursor from the previous response's `meta.pagination.next`. Omit for the first page. Send the same request body with it: a cursor that doesn't match the body you send is rejected with `invalid_cursor`.|
|body|body|[MetricsExploreRequest](#schemametricsexplorerequest)|true|none|
|» entity|body|object|true|Entity name for the metric to query. One metric per request. An unknown value, including `subscriptions` in sandbox, returns `unknown_entity`.|
|» from|body|string|true|RFC 3339 datetime string or `YYYY-MM-DD` date for the start of the range, interpreted at 00:00 UTC. Inclusive. Must be within the metric's `max_lookback_days`, otherwise Paddle returns `max_lookback_exceeded`.|
|» to|body|string|true|RFC 3339 datetime string or `YYYY-MM-DD` date for the end of the range, interpreted at 00:00 UTC. Exclusive. Clamped to the current time if in the future.|
|» measures|body|[[MetricsExploreMeasure](#schemametricsexploremeasure)]|true|One or more measures to compute.|
|» interval|body|object|false|Interval that results are bucketed by. Every query is bucketed, so each entry in `timeseries` carries a `timestamp`.|
|» dimensions|body|[string]|false|Dimensions to group results by. Each combination of values returns as a segment. `timestamp` is implied by `interval`, so don't include it here.|
|» filters|body|[[MetricsExploreFilter](#schemametricsexplorefilter)]|false|Filters to narrow results by dimension. Multiple filters are combined, so results must match all of them.|
|» order_by|body|[[MetricsExploreOrderBy](#schemametricsexploreorderby)]|false|Ordering. Required when you pass `dimensions`, because it decides which segments land on the page. Omitting it on a query with dimensions returns `invalid_field`.|
|» per_page|body|integer|false|Number of segments returned per page, not datapoints. Each segment carries its complete timeseries. Paddle returns the maximum if you request more, so check `meta.pagination.per_page` to see how many came back. A page can hold at most 10,000 datapoints (`per_page` multiplied by the time buckets in your range), otherwise Paddle returns `too_many_datapoints`.<br><br>Default: `5`; Maximum: `50`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "entity": "transactions.completed",
    "interval": "month",
    "currency_code": "USD",
    "starts_at": "2026-05-01T00:00:00Z",
```

## Get MRR (monthly recurring revenue) metrics

<a id="opIdget-metrics-monthly-recurring-revenue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.paddle.com/metrics/monthly-recurring-revenue?from=1970-01-01&to=1970-01-01' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /metrics/monthly-recurring-revenue`

Returns timeseries data for monthly recurring revenue in a given date range. Trends have a daily granularity.
Current monthly recurring revenue total. Includes new subscriptions, upgrades, downgrades and churn. Does not include one-time payments or deductions for Paddle fees.

When `to` and `from` are the same, returns an empty timeseries.

<h3 id="get-mrr-monthly-recurring-revenue-metrics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|from|query|string(date)|true|Return data from a specific date. Pass an RFC 3339 full-date string. Interpreted at 00:00 UTC. Must be before or the same as `to`.|
|to|query|string(date)|true|Return data up to a specific date. Pass an RFC 3339 full-date string. Interpreted as 00:00 UTC. Must be after or the same as `from`.|

> 200 Response

<h1 id="paddle-api-ip-addresses">IP addresses</h1>

IP addresses are the Paddle IP addresses for the environment that you make the request in. You can add them to your allowlist.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/ip-addresses">IP addresses overview</a>

## Get Paddle IP addresses

<a id="opIdget-ip-addresses"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/ips \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /ips`

Returns Paddle IP addresses. You can add these IP addresses to your allowlist.

IP addresses returned are for the environment that you're making the request in. For example, making the request to the production base URL returns all production IP addresses.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "ipv4_cidrs": [
      "34.194.127.46/32",
      "54.234.237.108/32",
      "3.208.120.145/32"
```

<h1 id="paddle-api-events">Events</h1>

Event entities describe something notable that happened in your Paddle system.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/events">Event entity overview</a>

## List events

<a id="opIdlist-events"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /events`

Returns a paginated list of events that have occurred in the last 90 days. Use the query parameters to page through results.

Events older than 90 days aren't retained.

This is sometimes referred to as "the event stream."

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/events/list-events">List events</a>

<h3 id="list-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `50`; Maximum: `200`.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Order returned entities by the specified field and direction (`[ASC]` or `[DESC]`). For example, `?order_by=id[ASC]`.<br><br>Valid fields for ordering: `id` (for `event_id`).|
|event_type|query|[[EventTypeName](#schemaeventtypename)]|false|Return events that match the specified event type. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple event types.|
|filter|query|string|false|Return entities that contain the value specified. Pass a Paddle ID or email address that appears in the event payload, or part of one. Complete Paddle IDs and email addresses match exactly; partial values match as a prefix or substring, and must be at least three characters.|
|to|query|string|false|Return entities up to a specific time. Pass an RFC 3339 datetime string.|
|from|query|string|false|Return entities from a specific time. Pass an RFC 3339 datetime string.|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

<h1 id="paddle-api-event-types">Event types</h1>

Event types are actions that Paddle creates events for.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/event-types">Event types overview</a>

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/event-types \
```

<h1 id="paddle-api-discounts">Discounts</h1>

Discount entities describe percentage or amount-based discounts for transactions. They're sometimes called coupons or promo codes.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/discounts">Discount entity overview</a>

## List discounts

<a id="opIdlist-discounts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/discounts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /discounts`

Returns a paginated list of discounts. Use the query parameters to page through results.

By default, Paddle returns discounts that are `active`. Use the `status` query parameter to return discounts that are archived.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/discounts/list-discounts">List discounts</a>

<h3 id="list-discounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|query|[string]|false|Return only the IDs specified. Use a comma-separated list to get multiple entities.|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `50`; Maximum: `200`.|
|include|query|[[DiscountIncludeEnum](#schemadiscountincludeenum)]|false|Include related entities in the response. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple entities.|
|code|query|[string]|false|Return entities that match the discount code. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple discount codes.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Order returned entities by the specified field and direction (`[ASC]` or `[DESC]`). For example, `?order_by=id[ASC]`.<br><br>Valid fields for ordering: `created_at` and `id`.|
|status|query|[[DiscountStatusQueryEnum](#schemadiscountstatusqueryenum)]|false|Return entities that match the specified status. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple status values.|
|mode|query|[DiscountModeQueryEnum](#schemadiscountmodequeryenum)|false|Return entities that match the specified mode.|
|discount_group_id|query|[string]|false|Return entities related to the specified discount group. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple discount group IDs.|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|include|discount_group|
|status|active|
|status|archived|
|mode|standard|
|mode|custom|

## Create a discount

<a id="opIdcreate-discount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/discounts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "All orders (10% off)",
    "type": "percentage",
    "amount": "10",
    "code": "BF10OFF",
    "enabled_for_checkout": true,
    "recur": true,
    "maximum_recurring_intervals": 3,
    "expires_at": "2024-12-03T00:00:00Z",
    "discount_group_id": "dsg_01js2gqehzccfkywgx1jk2mtsp"
  }'
```

`POST /discounts`

Creates a new discount.

If successful, your response includes a copy of the new discount entity.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/discounts/create-discount">Create a discount</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "All orders (10% off)",
  "type": "percentage",
  "amount": "10",
  "code": "BF10OFF",
  "enabled_for_checkout": true,
  "recur": true,
  "maximum_recurring_intervals": 3,
  "expires_at": "2024-12-03T00:00:00Z",
  "discount_group_id": "dsg_01js2gqehzccfkywgx1jk2mtsp"
```

<a id="opIdupdate-discount"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/discounts/string \

  }'
```

`PATCH /discounts/{discount_id}`

Updates a discount using its ID.

If successful, your response includes a copy of the updated discount entity.

To update a checkout recovery discount, configure your checkout recovery settings in the dashboard.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/discounts/update-discount">Update a discount</a>

```json
  "discount_group_id": "dsg_01js2gqehzccfkywgx1jk2mtsp"
```

<h1 id="paddle-api-discount-groups">Discount groups</h1>

Discount group entities let you organize your discounts by grouping them together.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/discount-groups">Discount Groups overview</a>

## List discount groups

<a id="opIdlist-discount-groups"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/discount-groups \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /discount-groups`

Returns a paginated list of discount groups. Use the query parameters to page through results.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/discount-groups/list-discount-groups">List discount groups</a>

<h3 id="list-discount-groups-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|query|[string]|false|Return only the IDs specified. Use a comma-separated list to get multiple entities.|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `50`; Maximum: `200`.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Order returned entities by the specified field and direction (`[ASC]` or `[DESC]`). For example, `?order_by=id[ASC]`.<br><br>Valid fields for ordering: `created_at` and `id`.|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

```json
      "id": "dsg_01gtf15svsqzgp9325ss4ebmwt",
      "name": "Black Friday 2024",
```

<h1 id="paddle-api-customer-portals">Customer portals</h1>

The customer portal lets customers manage their subscriptions, payment methods, and account information. Customer portal sessions hold authenticated links to the portal for a customer.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/customer-portals">Customer portals overview</a>

## Create a customer portal session

<a id="opIdcreate-customer-portal-session"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/customers/ctm_01grnn4zta5a1mf02jjze7y2ys/portal-sessions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "subscription_ids": [
      "sub_01h04vsc0qhwtsbsxh3422wjs4"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /customers/{customer_id}/portal-sessions`

Creates a customer portal session for a customer.

The [customer portal](https://developer.paddle.com/concepts/customer-portal) is a secure, Paddle-hosted site that allows
customers to manage their own subscriptions, payments, and account information without you having to build custom billing screens.

Customers can:

* View transaction history
* Download invoices
* Update payment methods
* Manage their subscriptions including making changes or cancellations
* Revise details on completed transactions

You can create a customer portal session to generate authenticated links for a customer
so that they're automatically signed in to the portal. It's typically used when linking to
the customer portal from your app where customers are already authenticated.

You can include an array of `subscription_ids` to generate authenticated portal links that let customers make
changes to their subscriptions. You can use these links as part of subscription management workflows rather than
building your own billing screens.

Customer portal sessions are temporary and shouldn't be cached.

The customer portal is fully hosted by Paddle. For security and the best customer experience, don't embed the customer
portal in an iframe.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/customer-portals/create-customer-portal-session">Create a customer portal session</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "subscription_ids": [
    "sub_01h04vsc0qhwtsbsxh3422wjs4"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-customer-portal-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer_id|path|[CustomerId](#schemacustomerid)|true|Paddle ID of the customer entity to work with.|
|body|body|[CustomerPortalSessionCreate](#schemacustomerportalsessioncreate)|true|none|
|» subscription_ids|body|[[SubscriptionId](#schemasubscriptionid)]|false|List of subscriptions to create authenticated customer portal deep links for.|

<h1 id="paddle-api-customers">Customers</h1>

Customer entities hold information about the people and businesses that make purchases. They're related to addresses and businesses.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/customers">Customer entity overview</a>

## List customers

<a id="opIdlist-customers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/customers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /customers`

Returns a paginated list of customers. Use the query parameters to page through results.

By default, Paddle returns customers that are `active`. Use the `status` query parameter to return customers that are archived.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/customers/list-customers">List customers</a>

<h3 id="list-customers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|query|[string]|false|Return only the IDs specified. Use a comma-separated list to get multiple entities.|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `50`; Maximum: `200`.|
|email|query|[string]|false|Return entities that exactly match the specified email address. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple email addresses. Recommended for precise matching of email addresses.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Order returned entities by the specified field and direction (`[ASC]` or `[DESC]`). For example, `?order_by=id[ASC]`.<br><br>Valid fields for ordering: `id`.|
|status|query|[[StatusQuery](#schemastatusquery)]|false|Return entities that match the specified status. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple status values.|
|search|query|string|false|Return entities that match a search query. Searches `id`, `name`, and `email` fields. Use the `email` query parameter for precise matching of email addresses.|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|archived|

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/customers \
```

`POST /customers`

Creates a new customer.

If successful, your response includes a copy of the new customer entity.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/customers/create-customer">Create a customer</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "jo@example.com",
  "name": "Jo Brown"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-customer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CustomerCreate](#schemacustomercreate)|true|none|
|» name|body|[Name](#schemaname) \| null|false|Full name of this customer. Required when creating transactions where `collection_mode` is `manual` (invoices).|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[Name](#schemaname)|false|Full name.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» email|body|object|true|Email address for this customer.|

## List credit balances for a customer

<a id="opIdlist-credit-balances"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/customers/ctm_01grnn4zta5a1mf02jjze7y2ys/credit-balances \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /customers/{customer_id}/credit-balances`

Returns a list of credit balances for each currency for a customer. Each balance has three totals:

* `available`: total available to use.
* `reserved`: total temporarily reserved for billed transactions.
* `used`: total amount of credit used.

Credit is added to the `available` total initially. When used, it moves to the `used` total.

The `reserved` total is used when a credit balance is applied to a transaction that's marked as `billed`, like when working with an issued invoice. It's not available for other transactions at this point, but isn't considered `used` until the transaction is completed. If a `billed` transaction is `canceled`, any reserved credit moves back to `available`.

Credit balances are created automatically by Paddle when you take an action that results in Paddle creating a credit for a customer, like making prorated changes to a subscription. An empty `data` array is returned where a customer has no credit balances.

The response is not paginated.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/customers/list-credit-balances">List credit balances for a customer</a>

<h3 id="list-credit-balances-for-a-customer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customer_id|path|[CustomerId](#schemacustomerid)|true|Paddle ID of the customer entity to work with.|
|currency_code|query|[string]|false|Return entities that match the currency code. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple currency codes.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "customer_id": "ctm_01gw9m680k848184fpttwr0b7z",
      "currency_code": "USD",
      "balance": {
        "available": "550",
        "reserved": "900",
        "used": "1300"
      }
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "request_id": "32cf1966-ed49-47d6-a76a-a9b8f7843245"
  }
}
```

## Generate an authentication token for a customer

<a id="opIdgenerate-customer-authentication-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/customers/ctm_01grnn4zta5a1mf02jjze7y2ys/auth-token \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /customers/{customer_id}/auth-token`

Generates an authentication token for a customer. You can pass a generated authentication token to Paddle.js when opening a checkout to let customers work with saved payment methods.

Authentication tokens are temporary and shouldn't be cached. They're valid until the `expires_at` date returned in the response.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/customers/generate-customer-authentication-token">Generate an authentication token for a customer</a>

<h3 id="generate-an-authentication-token-for-a-customer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

<h1 id="paddle-api-countries">Countries</h1>

Country entities describe the countries that Paddle knows about, including whether Paddle supports sales to customers there.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/countries">Countries overview</a>

## List Paddle countries

<a id="opIdlist-countries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/countries \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /countries`

automatic price conversion and whether Paddle supports sales to customers there.

<h1 id="paddle-api-client-tokens">Client tokens</h1>

Client token entities hold the details to authenticate Paddle.js in your frontend code.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/client-tokens">Client-side tokens entity overview</a>

## List client-side tokens

<a id="opIdlist-client-tokens"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/client-tokens \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /client-tokens`

Returns a paginated list of client-side tokens. Use the query parameters to [page through results](https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/about/pagination).

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/client-tokens/list-client-tokens">List client-side tokens</a>

<h3 id="list-client-side-tokens-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `50`; Maximum: `200`.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Order returned entities by the specified field and direction (`[ASC]` or `[DESC]`). For example, `?order_by=id[ASC]`.<br><br>Valid fields for ordering: `id`.|
|status|query|[[ClientTokensStatusQuery](#schemaclienttokensstatusquery)]|false|Return entities that match the specified status. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple status values.|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|revoked|

> Example responses

> 200 Response


## Create a client-side token

<a id="opIdcreate-client-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/client-tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Pricing page integration",
    "description": "Used to display prices and open checkout within our pricing page on our marketing domain."
  }'
```

`POST /client-tokens`

Creates a new client-side token.

If successful, your response includes a copy of the new client-side token entity.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/client-tokens/create-client-token">Create a client-side token</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Pricing page integration",
  "description": "Used to display prices and open checkout within our pricing page on our marketing domain."
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-client-side-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ClientTokenCreate](#schemaclienttokencreate)|true|none|
|» name|body|[ClientTokenName](#schemaclienttokenname)|true|Short name of this client-side token. Typically unique and human-identifiable.|
|» description|body|[ClientTokenDescription](#schemaclienttokendescription) \| null|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[ClientTokenDescription](#schemaclienttokendescription)|false|Short description of this client-side token. Typically gives details about what the token is used for and where it's used.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "ctkn_01ghbkd0frb9k95cnhwd1bxpvk",
```

## Update a client-side token

<a id="opIdupdate-client-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/client-tokens/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "status": "revoked"
  }'
```

`PATCH /client-tokens/{client_token_id}`

Updates a client-side token using its ID.

You can revoke a client-side token by changing its `status` to `revoked`. Client-side tokens that are revoked can't be updated to `active`.

If successful, your response includes a copy of the updated client-side token entity.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/client-tokens/update-client-token">Update a client-side token</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "status": "revoked"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_token_id|path|string|true|Paddle ID of the client-side token entity.|

<h1 id="paddle-api-checkout-domains">Checkout domains</h1>

Checkout domain entities hold the domains that you've submitted to serve Paddle Checkout for your account, and their approval status.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/checkout-domains">Checkout domains overview</a>

## List checkout domains

<a id="opIdlist-checkout-domains"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/checkout-domains \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /checkout-domains`

Returns a paginated list of checkout domains submitted for your account. Use the query parameters to page through results.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/checkout-domains/list-checkout-domains">List checkout domains</a>

<h3 id="list-checkout-domains-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|query|[string]|false|Return only the IDs specified. Use a comma-separated list to get multiple entities.|
|after|query|string|false|Return entities after the specified Paddle ID when working with paginated endpoints. Used in the `meta.pagination.next` URL in responses for list operations.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Set how many entities are returned per page. Paddle returns the maximum number of results if a number greater than the maximum is requested. Check `meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see how many were returned.<br><br>Default: `50`; Maximum: `200`.|
|domain|query|string|false|Filter results to include the specified fully qualified domain name (FQDN), its ancestors, and any of its subdomains. For example, if you provide `app.example.com`, the results include `app.example.com`, `example.com` and any subdomains such as `cool.app.example.com`.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Order returned entities by the specified field and direction (`[ASC]` or `[DESC]`). For example, `?order_by=id[ASC]`.<br><br>Valid fields for ordering: `id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`.|
|status|query|[[CheckoutDomainApprovalStatusQuery](#schemacheckoutdomainapprovalstatusquery)]|false|Return entities that match the specified status. Use a comma-separated list to specify multiple status values.|
|Skip-Count|header|string|false|Set to `true` to skip the count query on list operations. When set, `meta.pagination.estimated_total` returns `-1` instead of an exact count.|

|status|pending_review|

|status|in_review|
|status|action_required|

## Verify a payment method for a checkout domain

<a id="opIdverify-checkout-domain-payment-method"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.paddle.com/checkout-domains/string/verify-payment-method \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "payment_method": "apple_pay"
  }'
```

`POST /checkout-domains/{domain_id}/verify-payment-method`

Triggers payment method verification for a checkout domain. Currently supports Apple Pay only.

Before verifying, the checkout domain must be in `approved` status and the domain association file must be correctly hosted.

<a href="https://developer.paddle.com/api-reference/checkout-domains/verify-checkout-domain-payment-method">Verify a payment method for a checkout domain</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "payment_method": "apple_pay"
}
```
